- **BU-70 A published row names the Callable input an operation calls: `PublishedRow.Calls`; `truncate` and `removeAll` have rows**
  (2026-10-27, chosen 2026-10-31; PLAN G264 U0′, a Full change under WORKFLOW Q11: BU's design-first candidate and R4's prototype-first
  candidate (lane B), judged by the shared tests; R4-M150 stays U2's) SPEC 4.9.6 publishes Array `truncate` ("Destruction of the
  relevant `T`") and `removeAll` ("Calls of `matching`; destruction of the removed `T`") as rows, the operations' complete published
  effects, which callers use and never a library body; 15.6.4 composes the destruction a row lists at the call (R4's U2 reads
  `Destroys`); 8.11.4 composes a Callable argument's calls at the caller through the actual argument. `ArrayTruncate` had no row and
  `removeAll` no `KimiDeclarationId`, so A4 entered both bodies at every caller, and `PublishedRow` could not say "calls the Callable
  input", so a row for `removeAll` would have accepted a printing callback under `confined` (E1, E3).
  - The representation: `PublishedRow(Runs, On, Destroys, InPlace, Calls)`, `Calls` the parameter slot of the by-value Callable input whose
    calls the row publishes (-1 none), called through a shared borrow of it, the receiver its Callable premise declares (every 4.9.6
    "Calls of" row: `removeAll`, `sort(by:)`, `firstIndexWhere`), and destroyed after the last call (15.6.4, 16.3.3: a by-value input's
    cleanup is the callee's, as 8.11.4's owner acquisition destroys the remaining environment). `TyCtxt.Published`, where the row is formed,
    checks once, before it forms the first Calls row, that every Calls row's premise declares `ref` (`CheckCallsRows` through
    `Binding.CallableReceiver`; a violated catalog contract is an internal error); a later read costs what any row's does. Rows:
    `ArrayTruncate` `Target` (as `clear`), `ArrayRemoveAll` `CallsThenTarget` (`Destroys: 0, Calls: 1`; 4.9.7: destroyed after the last
    call). `KimiDeclarationId.ArrayRemoveAll` is one more ID (not a closed vocabulary; R5-M28's precedent).
  - Readers: `TyCtxt.Published` gives `Calls` to A4, where `MirEffects.Function` and `Enter` compose, after the row's `Runs` and
    `Destroys`, a call through the Type below that parameter (`Below`: the actual argument under the call's substitution, a Closure, a
    function item, an abstract input or a Function Type) with the shared receiver and that Type's destruction, through the one path a
    body's Value call uses (`Item`/`Process`). `Binding.PublishedOperations.SummarizePublishedOperation` reads the whole row from
    `TyCtxt.Published`, its requirement and its Callable input, and counts their effects as published, so both bodies are verified
    against their rows (`PublishedOperationBodiesStayWithinTheirRows`). The row's effects hold only for that check
    (`EffectSummary.CheckPublished`); a definition's own body is checked by `EffectSummary.CheckBody` (also a virtual function's), so
    `Check` takes no row and no mode parameter. A5 is unchanged: C3's guard (R4-M143) keeps W at both calls until U2.
  - The choice: both candidates pass 47 of the 48 shared rows on both pipelines at a cost within noise. Lane B has the same column but
    reads the receiver from the premise at every call and composes no destruction of the input, so its A4 accepts RmLoud, RmLoudLet,
    RmLoudLocal and PruneLoud (a by-value `matching` owning a value whose `drop` prints, under `confined`), which the bodies and
    Binding reject: unsound.
  - Rejected: an A4 rule calling every by-value input whose Type is a Callable-bounded parameter at a published operation's call (a
    consumer deciding by the callee's shape what the catalog should publish); keeping A4 in the two bodies with only `Destroys`
    published (a row half read); a receiver column (no 4.9 row calls its input otherwise); lane B's receiver read from the premise at
    each call (the declaration's fact read again per call); lane B's row without the input's destruction (unsound, above).
  - Consequences: A4 gets E1/E3/E5/E7 through the rows, not the bodies; no A5 verdict changes; the retention rows are unchanged (a row
    changes no retention row, BU-42, BU-47). Binding's old effect check, `EffectSummary`, whose records every pipeline publishes
    (R5-M156), still enters the bodies at callers (its `Target` keys `ArrayClear` and `Replace`) until R6-check deletes it. A4 reports
    `OwnershipDepthLimit_Kd` for `truncate` or `removeAll` on an Array whose element is a 32-deep struct chain, where the bodies
    accepted, as `clear`'s row already does: `Destroys` names the container, so the walk meets the element one level deeper; a located
    limit that misses no effect, open with that column. Open: SPEC 4.9.6's `removeAll` row does not name the destruction of `matching`,
    which this row composes by 15.6.4's by-value sentence (equal to the body's effects); whether 4.9.6's text names it is the owner's.

- **BU-68 A local's failed Origin clause leaves Unbound only the inference variables it names** (2026-10-31; PLAN G306 (1), unit bu85
  U1) SPEC 15.3.3: a local's clauses are checks that assume nothing (ExtractOriginPremises never reads them), so only the slots a
  failed clause feeds can rest on it; SPEC 23.1.2: every other failed requirement is reported. Path a made every owner's failed clause
  a contract's: `Relations.Clear()`, State 3, every pending slot Unbound, which hid a local's independent records.
  - The fact: `OriginDeclaration.FailedClauses`, the bound Origins of each failed clause, null where an operand is unavailable. One
    writer, `FailOriginClause` (the clause loop's failure arm); its readers are the completion (`FailOriginDeclaration`,
    `RestsOnFailedClause`) and, later, G306 U2's dependence query. A reused list, allocated at a declaration's first failed clause and
    cleared by `Reset`; a warm rebind allocates nothing.
  - The rule (`Binding.OriginDeclarations.Failures.cs`): for a local (`OriginDeclaration.IsLocal`, the one discriminator JudgeLocalClause
    also reads) whose failed clauses each name a bound Origin, a pending slot that one of them names, resolved through the declaration's
    equalities, stays Unbound and rests on the first failed clause (`PendingFailure`, path a); every other slot completes by the
    ordinary rule, the bound clauses stay and are judged, and the owner still fails on its first failed clause. A failed clause that
    names no bound Origin, and a contract's failed clause, make the whole declaration unavailable as before. The scope is decided once,
    at completion: no second walk and no per-binder lookup (R4-M118's rejected route).
  - Limit: a failed operand names no slot, also one that fails on the declaration's own set (a repeated set's `x.a`, a missing member
    `x.zz`). Where a `==` repair would have substituted such a slot, its completion can differ from the repaired program's, so at most
    a dependent record is reported as direct, never a record lost (BU-61's stance).
  - BU-62: `PendingFailure` keeps its one writer and its meaning; for a local, path a now leaves only the named slots Unbound, and they
    still rest on the failed clause (`UnboundCause`). `Failure` stays set, so `FailedOriginEnvironment` still derives a failed fit
    beneath the local.
  - Records: x-valid-clause-beside gains UnsatisfiedOriginRelation_Kd at `P.init(a, l@ref)`; i-unrelated-slot's and u1-typo-slot's
    `p.q` go Unproven to Unsatisfied; each is its valid twin's. The named slot rests, unchanged, in x-named-later, i-named-slot,
    x-upper-failed, x-eq-beside, m3 and meet-ret. Only incomplete compilations change.
  - Rejected: resting every slot of a local (the cause above); a failure lookup per binder (R4-M118).

  - Superseded in part by BU-159 (2026-11-11, H11b-0 B1): no failed clause makes the whole declaration unavailable any more ("A
    failed clause that names no bound Origin, and a contract's failed clause, make the whole declaration unavailable as before"); a
    failed clause fails only itself, and this entry's named-slot rule holds for every owner.
- **BU-69 A fixed-fixed fit record rests on a failed contract only when that contract could prove it** (2026-10-31; PLAN G306 (3), unit
  bu85 U2; R4 agreed to the partial supersession of R4-M133 on three conditions; supersedes in part BU-62's premise contract and
  R4-M133's clause "a failure no chain refutes in a failed Origin environment a dependent of it") SPEC 23.1.2: a failed fit is a
  dependent only of a failure whose repair could remove it. FailedOriginEnvironment derived every non-refuted record under any failed
  ancestor without asking whether that contract could have proven it, which hid independent records (a-base-method, a-fn-clause) and,
  one way, published dependent ones (r-fn-other).
  - The contract: a failed contract's bound clauses (`RejectedRelations`) and its failed clauses' bound Origins with their direction (on
    `OriginDeclaration`) are read only by dependence queries. A dependence query decides whether a relation that already failed is
    derived, so it only ever removes a dependent report: the declaration judge's rows and the fit judge's records with no Unbound end.
    The fit judge's query reads them wherever the premise extraction reads that contract (R1 and a Type's premises, substituted); the
    declaration judge reads the bound clauses at R1 only (the limit below). Each judge's own requests read them; a request nested in
    their extraction (a capability proof whose summary is kept, for one) and every other request still see the contract unavailable.
    The state is `readingFailedContracts`, the premise depth of the judges' own requests, in `Binding.OriginPremises.cs` (the premise
    component), set by both judges, replacing Chains.cs's `judgingDeclarationRows`; it outlives R6-check, since fixed-fixed fit
    records stay Binding's until R7.
  - The query (`DependenceCause`, Binding.OriginDeclarations.Failures.cs; R4's conditions): decided once, where the record is formed
    (RecordOriginChains), as its typed cause; no consumer re-runs a proof to decide or explain it. One premise extraction at the use,
    run only for a failed record with no Unbound end (that one keeps the ancestor walk, R4-M118, until R6-check). The record is derived
    iff, under its Semantics condition (`OriginRelationFact.Condition`), the premises with the failed contracts' bound clauses entail it,
    added contract by contract (the cause: that contract's failed clause), or one repair of a failed clause does (the cause: that
    clause): `L outlives ?` when longer >= L; `? outlives L` when L >= shorter and longer outlives an Origin visible at the clause; `==`
    either; a clause with no bound Origin or a guessed operator when longer outlives a visible Origin. Visible: `static`, a declared
    Origin of the failed declaration or of one enclosing it, an Origin argument of the occurrence. An `==` record is derived only when
    both directions are.
  - Limits: repairs are judged one failed clause at one read at a time, so t2-bridge (one Type clause's repair at two occurrences) and
    n2-combo (two contracts' repairs together) publish an extra dependent report, never hiding an error. The declaration judge reads R1
    only: no declaration row reaching a failed Type's premises was found, so that read stays the fit query's.
  - Records: Unproven like their twins at a-base-method, a-base-method-dep, a-fn-clause, a-fn-out-indep, r-dir-left, r-m-unnameable,
    r-m-whole, r-nest-unnameable, n2-indep, m2-indep, g-guessed-method and c-store-failed (`ClosureEnvironmentOriginTest`'s
    FailedClauseStore gains UnprovenOriginRelation_Kd `p`); derived like their repairs: r-fn-other, t2-same, t2-static, as-fail,
    t2-cross.
  - Rejected: one walk over enclosing declarations only (a contract reaching the use through a Type's premises); a repair ranging over
    every Origin (an enclosing contract's clause cannot name a nested signature's own Origins).
  - Superseded in part by BU-159 (2026-11-11, H11b-0 B1): the dependence query's reads of a failed contract's bound clauses
    (`RejectedRelations`), since they are premises already. Its repairs stay.

- **BU-71 Binding publishes each interned Type's height, `BoundType.Height`, and each substitution's, `Subst.Height`** (2026-10-31;
  PLAN G332, unit bu91; the owner approved G332 and this entry together, verbatim 「まとめて承認します」) SPEC-neutral: a measure of the Type
  term, which no language rule reads.
  - Representation: one int per BoundType, set in its constructor from its children's heights beside the other subtree summaries; no
    walk. A leaf (a Primitive, the wrapping Scalar included, a struct without arguments, a Type parameter) is 0; any other Type is 1 + the
    greatest height of its children, the parts its identity holds as Types: its components (Type arguments, Tuple components, a fixed
    array's element, a referent or pointee, a Function Type's inputs and result, a function item's Type arguments, a projection's self
    and Contract Type, a Closure's environment) and a Closure's whole ClosureContext, one child of height `Subst.Height`: computed on
    read as the greatest height over its Types, Self and Declaring (one read each), 0 for none. Lengths and Origins are no Types and no
    children. So a Closure with no environment is 0 without a context and 1 under an identity context (one binding only leaves).
  - Reason: G332's recurrence rule asks whether a key's Type grows (type-driven keys stop past height 128, a body counts a generation
    only on substitution-height growth). The collector lacked the fact; its owner publishes it (AGENTS), with no collector table.
  - One fact, one owner: Binding's growth guards read it. `Binding.CapabilityTypeDepth` and its memo table `capabilityTypeDepths` are
    deleted; the capability proof's growth step (BU-22) and the component summary's re-entry test (SPEC 8.3.3) compare `Height`. The
    old depth was the components-only height + 1, so it differs only on a Closure's context; the related classes and the diagnostic
    snapshot are unchanged. `OwnershipAnalysis.TypeDepth`, the old Analysis's copy, goes with that Analysis at R6-check (D5 freeze).
  - Two facts, two child lists: ContainsParameter, ContainsPairLayer and HasAbstractPart read only BU-60's held instance, since they ask
    what a substitution may rewrite and the walks rewrite only that instance, keeping a context a function's instance made (R5-M36,
    ClosePart). Height measures the term as interned, whose identity holds the whole context: a capture-free Closure in g<T> has no
    components, yet its instances' heights follow T. Those three summaries are unchanged.
  - Readers: G332's collector (R5) and Binding's two growth guards; R4's G349 and BU's G309-R may read it later.
  - Rejected: the held instance alone as a Closure's child (a key holding a capture-free Closure would never pass 128 however its
    instance grows); a table in the collector (a consumer computing its owner's fact); a stored Subst height (+8 B per Subst, for a
    read that costs one load per bound Type).

- **BU-72 Binding publishes the Type identity a member or element access was resolved through, `HirTables.IdentityPremise`**
  (2026-10-31; temporary; unit bu94; the owner, verbatim 「(a) 今行う」, on "BU publishes the identity-premise fact before C3, and R5 does
  the interim G168b now")
  - Fact: on a `MemberAccessKoto` (a Field, a Tuple element, any member) or an `IndexKoto` whose receiver's Type, through its
    Semantics layers, is a Type parameter P that the scope's identity premises make a complete Type U (SPEC 8.2.3, a chain `T is U`,
    `U is Pair` included), the node's plan row (`Second`, unused on these classes) holds the interned `BoundConstraint` `P is U`:
    TypeIdentity, Subject P, RequiredType U, the Type Binding resolved the access on. Null otherwise: no premise, a non-identity
    premise (a Contract, `T is Pick`), or a parameter nested in the receiver's Type (`xs: ref/Array<T>` with `T is Pair`: `xs[i]` is
    resolved on `Pair` through `xs`'s substitution, so neither `xs[i]` nor `xs[i].a` has the fact).
  - Writer: `Binding.PublishIdentityPremise`, called once where `BindAndAdaptNode` substitutes the receiver's Type (no second walk;
    the receiver may be parenthesized). The index pass clears it (`Binding.ClearIdentityPremise`), so each pass, a warm rebind
    included, publishes it again. The constraint is interned in the compilation's table: a direct premise's own object, or for a
    chain (`T is U`, `U is Pair`) a new derived `T is Pair`, made at the first pass and retained across passes; warm Bind 0 B.
  - Reader: R5's G168b MIR-builder guard. Where a projection's receiver Place has a Type parameter P through its Layers, it reads
    `HirTables.IdentityPremise(node)`, requires Subject == P and checks the projected shape on RequiredType against the node's Meaning
    (an Array's or fixed array's element, the Tuple element at the node's Folded position, a stored Field of the node's symbol) before
    its located `Unsupported_Kd`; it never infers the identity from a Type mismatch.
  - Reason: the premises sit in Binding's internal `ConstraintEnvironment`, availability is the private `AvailableConstraintFact`,
    and Meaning carries only the substitution's result. The access's existing plan row carries the fact; no table.
  - Removal: when G170's identity query lands, when TyCtxt answers the identical Type under premises and the projection gets its
    Type; the writer, its reset, the reader and this entry go. Each is `[Transitional("R4")]`, G170's stage (its R4-exit row).
- **BU-73 A callable's fixed signature Origins are Owned parts; an erasure judges its environment; one atom walk with a binder class**
  (2026-11-02; PLAN G353, unit bu100; the owner, 2026-10-31, verbatim 「G353 の設計 今すぐ設計だけ始める で決定します」 and 「G353：サポートの縮小を認める」) SPEC 15.2.3,
  7.7.4, 8.10, 11.6, 15.3.4, 15.8.2.
  - Fixed signature Origins (SPEC 15.2.3): the Origins of a callable's call signature other than its per-call ones, which are exactly
    the omitted Origins of its direct borrowed parameters (SPEC 8.10), its receiver ρ and its call result (15.8.2). Written `during`
    Origins, enclosing atoms, Type arguments' Origins and an anonymous function's nested borrow-layer and aggregate-slot parameter
    Origins (body inference variables, fixed once, 15.3.4) are fixed. Nothing enters a Type's identity, Height or held context.
  - One rule, `SignatureCapability`: a callable signature is an Owned part with its own per-call Origins closed to static
    (`SubstituteStoredOrigins` with `PerCallImages`: the direct inputs, ρ and the result), never the aggregate inputs. `CallSignature`
    gives the rows: a Function Type quantifying an input is its own signature under its syntax, and its verdict is the closed
    signature's, since it stores nothing else.
  - The erasure's subject, `ErasureSubject`: SPEC 7.7.4's complete environment, a Closure's captures as one Tuple (`TyCtxt.Tuple` over
    its Components, no copy), a Function Item itself. The required Function Type states the signature, so the erasure never judges it;
    the Tuple's members are the capture indices, so `OwnedMember` and r2-1b's ErasureOutcome read it unchanged.
  - One atom walk, `FixedAtoms` (R4-M159's Collect): the atoms of a binder class that a Type names, in first-occurrence order (its
    Components gated by `CarriesAnyOrigin || ContainsClosure`, and each Closure part's `ClosureSignature` at any depth, one
    `visitedParts` query), returning the first Closure part, outermost, through which it met one. `BinderClass` is closed:
    `EnclosingAnonymous` (an anonymous function enclosing the subject, ClosureType's Origin arguments) and `EnclosingContainer` (a
    container enclosing it). Enclosure is the ancestry test (`IsWithin`). The walk visits every part, keeping the first Closure part
    reached. For `EnclosingAnonymous` the descent adds nothing: a nested Closure's enclosing atoms are already its Origin arguments,
    and its own atoms do not enclose the subject. `IsWithin(subject, binder)` there is a no-op on Collect's walk: by R4-M159's
    invariant an atom of a Closure that does not enclose the subject reaches its signature only through a Type that passed its
    maker's call, which images it, so every anonymous atom the signature names, its own excepted, is an enclosing Closure's; it keeps
    the descent's nested Closures' own atoms (and those of Closures between them and the subject) out.
  - The Field rule (U2a; amends R4-M159): `BindPropertyHeader`, the one producer of an inferred stored Property Type (SPEC 11.6),
    refuses one holding a Closure (`ContainsClosure`) whose signature names an enclosing container's Origin (its Origin parameters,
    inherited ones included, directly or as an image): FixedAtoms' reached part for `EnclosingContainer`, the first Closure literal,
    outermost, at any depth, is one located `Unsupported_Kd` (`UnimagedClosure`). Imaging it would give these Types Origin arguments,
    which the old Analysis' `SupportsType` stops on (K5 would grow); a valid form no common rule covers stays `Unsupported_Kd`.
  - Rest (SPEC 23.1.2): the refusal is one fact on `BoundProperty` (`Refusal`, the literal), written with the Type each pass. The
    Property keeps its Type (withholding it fails SPEC 11.6's deadline with `UnprovenConstraint_Kd`). The Property-use site
    (`BindReference`) consults it and completes without a Type, as for a Type-less Property (x1's path), so a read, a call, an
    erasure, a typed `let` or an argument adds no record; the container's own facts rest through BU-22's rule on its failed stored
    Type. Each form gives one record, at the literal (a composite initializer's failure was not direct).
  - The support reduction (the owner, 2026-10-31, verbatim 「G353：サポートの縮小を認める」): valid forms dev accepted become
    `Unsupported_Kd`: L2h, L2j, L2k, N1, N3, N3c, N3e, R4's f4c, R2 (pass-move), R3 (copy-out), h2 and O5 (inherited). Dev's unsound
    acceptances close: L2g, m2 and both f4m. Dev's records become the one `Unsupported_Kd`: L2i, N1b, N3d, f4d, R1, h1, and the
    correct `UnprovenOriginRelation_Kd` of m1, v1 and v2. Two consequences: m1 loses its independent `UnprovenOriginRelation_Kd` at
    `w@move`, which `data` alone causes (keeping it needs a variance producer that skips a refused Field, a new mechanism: a stated
    limit until imaging); and the old Analysis stops after a Binding error, so an unrelated function's Loan conflict is unpublished on
    both pipelines (n5; the old Analysis' records are published on both until R6-check), as after any Binding `Unsupported_Kd`. On the mir ledger A5's `UnprovenOriginRelation_Kd` stands
    beside m1, v1 and v2, dependent on the refused Field (R4's own item).
  - Removal condition (PLAN, after R6-check): ClosureType's binder class takes containers, the Field read images them through the
    storage substitution, and `TypeOrigins.AccumulateRequirements` reads a Closure's arguments through `OriginArgumentVariance`, so
    `ClosureArgumentVariance` publishes the Field Closure's occurrences; then `UnimagedClosure`, `BoundProperty.Refusal` and its read
    go.
  - The Closure row (U2b): `CallSignature`'s Closure row is `ClosureSignature` under its definition, and a Closure's Owned verdict
    combines its captures with `SignatureCapability`, a part published as member `Components.Count` (outside −1 and 0..n−1; the
    erasure, judging `ErasureSubject`, never reads it). New rejections, correct under SPEC 15.2.3, each `UnprovenConstraint_Kd` at the
    use on both pipelines: the j group (j, a, e, p3b, p4-p7: a Closure naming an enclosing function's Origin, written, through a maker,
    a generic pass, an Option or the result; e's only record is now Binding's, before the old Analysis' R4-M159 stop), p10 (a generic
    maker's `func (x: T) => ()`, SPEC 8.15), q1, q2 (a nested or aggregate parameter's Origin, SPEC 15.3.4) and a method's Closure
    naming its container's Origin (m2 `source`, m3 `self.source`); the twins b, h, k, p8, p10b, q1s, q2s stay accepted. K5 does not
    grow; no library or milestone program is newly rejected. Like any Binding `UnprovenConstraint_Kd`, a new rejection stops the old
    Analysis, so another function's record is unpublished on both pipelines (m4 loses a `TransferRequired_Kd`, as dev does beside
    any such record, z1). Closes G353 and G273's named-function item.
  - The BU-60 gap row: where BU-60's view withholds a Closure's held instance (an Origin position closed in no instance, PLAN G300),
    `CallSignature` gives no signature and the part answers BU-22's limit with a site whose Use is the literal (`CapabilityWork.Site`,
    kept across passes); at the outermost scope it is Error and the prologue publishes the one located `Unsupported_Kd`, with no
    `UnprovenConstraint_Kd` added. A Closure Type whose literal's header did not bind (the Type BindConcreteClosure starts with) has no
    signature either, so its use rests on the literal's own failure (or gets the located `Unsupported_Kd` there), never on its captures
    alone; a Closure Type naming no literal is a broken contract.
  - Cost: one closed signature per Closure proven Owned, one Tuple per erased Closure; warm Bind 0 B.
  - Rejected: imaging a container's atoms in the Closure Type now (option (B): K5 grows until R6-check); a second walk for the record's
    location; an open `Func` filter, which reads as a mode.
- **BU-74 A recorded argument part's relation to its call is one published column, `ArgumentPart.Relation` (`CallRelation`)**
  (2026-11-01; PLAN G216 (a) Part 1 U1.6g3a and U1.6g3b; the owner's 「U1.6g3 をどうしますか？ 続ける」, 2026-10-31) The owner's rule: ArgumentKinds
  publishes a part's relation to its call as one fact, and no consumer infers that relation from BoundType or BindingState. G1b B4 (a
  consumer read "awaits its call" from the raw record and BindingState) and the U1.6g3 stop (ConflictWaits read "its call completed
  parts" from BoundType, HoldsCompletedPart, which a nested join's step 3 also satisfies during classification) share that cause: the
  relation was inferred, not published.
  - The fact: `CallRelation`, a [Flags] byte, the third column of the existing record, `ArgumentPart(Kind, Default, Relation)`, keyed
    and cleared with the kind; no table. `Awaits`, per part: its producer recorded it as awaiting its call. `Taken`, on a call
    argument's own record (created if absent, reading as an absent one): its call has selected and takes it.
  - Writers, one per bit (both through the one `ref` accessor `PartRecord`): `RecordPart`, the producers' one writer, writes Awaits by
    one row, every recorded kind awaits but Literal, and keeps Taken (ClassifiedByCall and DeferNestedCall re-record the probe while
    DecideTaken decides it again). It replaces Awaits' kind list `not (Typed or Literal or Aggregate)`; no producer records Typed or
    Aggregate, so the bit holds exactly where that test held. `SlotSolution.Default` records a Literal through RecordPart and adds its
    default, so it keeps only Taken. `TakeArgument`, called only by CompleteWaiting at the head of its loop, before IsWaiting,
    TakeWaiting and DecideTaken, writes Taken.
  - Readers, one per bit: `Awaits(core, record)`, for AwaitsCall, AwaitedKind and KindOf: the bit while the core is unbound and has no
    failure of its own. A join's step 3 may bind the part while its call classifies the argument (SPEC 14.9.2), so binding is not
    completion. `TakenByCall`, for ConflictWaits: decision (i)'s premise, "the call has selected", replacing HoldsCompletedPart (its
    BoundType walk and its copy of the awaiting kinds are deleted). Taken ends no Awaits: TryCandidate's re-check reads KindOf after
    CompleteWaiting, so a taken Join argument stays Join, and a taken Literal or Typed argument does not start awaiting.
  - ResultPropagation's `Completed` decided position waiting (a waited source whose parts are bound since, by its call or its join's
    step 3), not a call relation: gated by Taken, 11 rows keep a lone PrerequisiteUnavailable_Kd (SPEC 23.1.2). U1.6g3b renames it
    `BoundSince` under that contract ("complete" is the call's word). Deferred's `AwaitsFor || BoundSince` still reconstructs position
    waiting from BoundType; that is PLAN G335's open issue (position waiting published once per join).
  - Rejected: a side table read by one consumer; Taken per part (HoldsCompletedPart's walk again); Taken ending Awaits (above); a Taken
    mark at a Case construction (InferPayloads binds its payloads at their Types, so ConflictWaits is never reached there).

- **BU-75 A site whose own check fails because a part it judged failed is a derived failure** (2026-11-01; PLAN G216 (a) U2.1, r2-1b's
  fix; BU's bu95; the owner's option (B), 「推奨どおり」, 2026-11-01) SPEC 23.1.2.
  - The rule: a site whose own check fails (it computed a failing verdict: a fit, a proof, a conversion) because a part it judged
    failed, wherever that part is, is a derived failure: `Fail` plus a part prerequisite, classified by IsDerived, with no record.
    Fail's Invalid survives the site's completion, and the publisher's Rejected folds the site as an Error node (R4-M109 unchanged, not
    extended). A node that only read a part that did not resolve rests by consultation (`CompleteDependent` or a consultation frame),
    and the publisher keeps its Op (R4-M88). The site decides locally: its own verdict failed on a failed part, or it only consulted one.
  - Precondition: the part the site rests on is Invalid, so IsDerived's existing row (InvalidConstraint whose part is Invalid)
    classifies it; any other case is a broken contract, `InternalInvariant_Kd`. IsDerived is not widened. It is checked where every
    producer's node has failed: in Binding.Check's Final prologue (BU-76).
  - First site: `FailOwnedConversion` (`FailDerived`). An Owned failure that no work judged rests on the subject's failed operand
    context (`InvalidOperandContext`: its cause when Invalid, else the failed declaration, Invalid by construction); an Error's held
    cause rests on the node its producer holds (BU-76). They were `InternalInvariant_Kd` and a `CompleteDependent` rest, which
    `BindVariableCore`'s and the `return`'s completions overwrite, so MIR built a Resolved node over an invalid Type.
  - Open: an Owned proof that reads a field or payload Type left unresolved inside a Resolved declaration (PLAN G354 (3)).
  - Rejected: folding every final-pass dependent node as Error (it loses independent A1/A5 records, against R4-M88, R5-M63 and G121);
    UnprovenConstraint (an IsDerived case for one site); widening IsDerived and the context walk to Unresolved parts (prototype C moved
    nothing).

- **BU-76 A held cause names a node its owner fails by the end of Binding.Check's Final prologue** (2026-11-01; PLAN G216 (a) U2.1,
  r2-1b B1, bu97 U1; the owner's option (1), 「推奨どおり (1)」, 「(1) で進める」; bu97 U2: option 2, the owner's 「2. 段の一覧を公開し、prologue で確定する」,
  「推奨どおり (2)」) SPEC 8.3.3, 23.1.2.
  - The Owned walk holds the node it reads: a stored Type that failed, or its failed operand context (`InvalidOperandContext`, the
    walk and predicate of `OperandContexts`). An Owned leaf is never Error, so the leaf's Error branch is deleted.
  - Every held cause is a candidate list (ICheckCause: `Use` is its first candidate, `Next` the next): a node, a summary, a site or a
    conformance path is a list of one; a summary holding hops carries their list.
  - At a re-entry the walk holds the hops `ContractType` resolved through (`ResolutionHops`, outermost first, whose candidates are the
    hops' clauses). ContractTypes publishes each answer's hops (bu97 U2 unit a): a projection resolved by a specification adds its
    conformance path to its subject's (component 0's) hops, a specification with no path forwards its subject's hops, and any other
    answer has none; its memo (`contractParts`, BU-64) and batch (`Normalized`) values carry the (image, hops) pair, written by the run
    that made the image, so a hit never resolves again; the chains are interned per (path, step, inner) for the Binding's lifetime, as the
    paths they name. The settle points a use at the first hop whose clause failed by the prologue, the prerequisite its derived fact
    names.
    - By SPEC 8.3.3 some hop revisits itself and fails with its own record.
    - By SPEC 23.1.2 any failed hop gives the same records.
    - If none failed, the use rests on the re-entry's site, which the settle fails as FailNeededSites fails a site (BU-22, bu97 unit
      c″); a summary carries the site (`ReentrySite`) as it carries its candidates. Every re-entry has hops: an identity step is no
      re-entry (BU-22).
    - Each hop carries the projection step it resolved, and that step is the one WalkProjection tests (bu97 unit c′).
  - A limit holds its Use. The prologue fails it (PublishNeededLimits, then FailNeededSites) and Check's loop publishes and counts it
    once; a site only the loop's checks need is recorded after the loop (PublishSites). The erasure that holds a limit runs in body
    binding, earlier (FailOwnedConversion's only caller is RecordMismatch).
  - FailDerived lists the use, and the prologue settles it (`SettleDerivedUses`, after FailNeededSites): a part that is not Invalid is
    `InternalInvariant_Kd`, except a re-entry's site (above). The list is a temporary structure, separate from `specificationLinks` (that one chooses the node a
    conformance use rests on; this one checks a precondition). Removal condition: the erasure's Owned failure is decided after the
    prologue. An entry carries its held cause (none for an operand context, recorded at once); the settle reads only its candidates
    and never replaces a part another site recorded first (BU-61); the contract and removal condition are unchanged. FailDerived
    snapshots the held cause's candidates at failure (its Use and Next) and its ReentrySite.
  - Rejected:
    - naming the outer stored Type (r-opt);
    - naming the binding's Type node (not kept per path);
    - re-resolving the projection to find the path (it re-runs resolution);
    - a Language record for a broken contract;
    - IsDerived reading PartFailed (G354 (3) stays open);
    - one list with `specificationLinks` (another contract);
    - the innermost hop (ch: W:Has2 is valid); a hop read at resolution time (it fails only at the Definition deadline); a single-hop
      limit (option 1); a candidate facet only one cause kind implements.

- **BU-77 FailedFit: the evidence walk publishes, per candidate, each unbound failed part it meets and the candidate's pattern there**
  (2026-11-01; PLAN G216 (a) Part 1 U1.6h-1): superseded by BU-79 (2026-11-02); full text: 4fb6fcdb1.

- **BU-78 A failed source takes no part in its join: its join rests on it at its verdict, and a failed part makes its position wait**
  (superseded in part by BU-79: B4 / fix (a) and the FailedFit readers) (2026-11-01; PLAN G216 (a) Part 1 U1.6h-3' (3 + 3'); design
  revision 4; the owner's 「改訂 4でGO！」 and 「(1) 3′ で進める」) Amends U1.6d: a failed source of a join that waits for its position fits every
  candidate as a source, not as its whole join (SPEC 23.1.2, 10.4, 10.5.1, 14.9.2). It covers joins their call classifies; a typed join
  that decides by itself is not covered (PLAN).
  - Site 1, the verdict: RestOn records the cause during classification and decides nothing. `DecideRest`, the one writer of
    Dependent, writes the verdict when the join decides (DecideResult; DecideWaiting under a failed position). Conflict prevails.
  - Sites 2 and 6 (U1.6h-4): a failed source takes no part in whether its join's sources await (SourcesAwait, BoundSince), and a
    waited source that fails when its join decides (BindWaitedSources) is the join's cause (RestOn), so g192's J1 takes twice's Item
    Type from twice alone and J2's anonymous source fails at it on its own.
  - Site 3: a failed part makes its position Call, Waiting under 10.5.1 (PositionKind). Supersedes BU-43 R6's "`PositionKind`'s row is
    deleted (a classified join holds no failed part)" and "a nested join with a failed part decides at once". The reason they rested
    on no longer holds: a join with a failed part was Dependent at once, one failed part, so no classified join held one. Now
    Dependent is written only at the verdict, so a classified, waiting join holds failed parts, and PositionKind regains a row with
    a new meaning: Waiting, not "takes no part".
  - Site 4 (U1.6h-5): a join its survey left unclassified (no Literal record: a failed or unknown source beside its literals) is a Join
    (ClassifiedByCall), so its call classifies and selects.
  - Amended (G368 (1), 2026-11-06): a join that holds a typed part (`ResultContext.HasTyped`: its survey found one at any depth, or a
    collected source is one) and a failed source fixes no complete Type without its call (SPEC 10.5.1). As its call's control-flow
    argument it is its call's Join (ClassifiedByCall, by the one exit DecideResult shares with ConflictWaits, which a conflict takes
    first), so the call selects with the failed part a wildcard. A typed join nested in it still rests at its verdict; when the root
    binds it at the selected Type, its bound sources keep their records (BindWaitedSources, as DecideWaiting's contract and rule W
    say; a Conflict join's own record stands for its sources). Covered: named and value calls, Tuple and array elements, a failed
    operator source, and typed joins nested at any depth, also when every typed part lies in them. Sites 2 and 6 hold: g192 is
    unchanged, and g192t2 to g192t4 add J1's `twice` at `(bool) -> bool` (independent: the no-failure twin is NoApplicable). The
    records it adds are rule W's dependent ones (BU-79): Ambiguous or UnboundTypeArgument where site 3 leaves the position without
    evidence (the six `*_typed_fov` gate rows, g129, g251, i4, and v22, whose typed evidence comes from failed sources); and an inner
    literal or waiting call that fits the tree's own Type, met at the selected one (`5` and `identity(4)` in t7, t8 and the four
    `fp2_*_{inlit,deferred}_typed_fb` gate rows). Not covered (PLAN G368 (1)): a resting join outside a call (a local's use, an
    operator, A5's Loans); a tree whose typed parts are only borrows or function references nested beside failed sources, which the
    survey does not type (j1, j2).
  - U1.6d as amended (Part 1): a failed source of a join its call classifies fits every candidate as a source, not as its whole join.
    Its argument and its position are Waiting (10.5.1); its join records it as its cause and rests on it at its verdict (DecideRest).
    The evidence walk publishes the candidate's pattern at each unbound failed part (FailedFit, BU-77, with fix (b)); an ambiguity
    rests on it only where kept candidates' Types differ there, and an unsolved slot only when every one occurs at one; an unselected
    call publishes only the verdicts its waiting join judged and links every other part to them (fix (a)). Only unbound failed parts
    are covered; a typed one is decided at the merge into U2.1.
  - B4 and fix (a) below are superseded by BU-79 (rule W): only a held join's own Conflict report stays (ReportHeldConflicts).
  - B4 and fix (a), the unselected call's completion (CompleteUnselectedPart's one row, PublishJudged): a held join judged Conflict
    writes its own record once (`FailJudged`, the record's one form, shared with DecideWaiting). A held waiting join rests through its
    verdict (`DecideRest`) on its recorded Cause, or else on the verdict it lies under. Every other unbound part of the tree with no
    cause of its own (PartFailed, HasFailureCauses) rests on the nearest judged verdict, by the join tree JudgeHeld walks, from the
    outermost form that delivers each waited source (`ResultSourceForm`, the result-source walk's delivery chain that ResultTarget
    reads). Nothing is bound and no default is taken.
  - Rejected: a call resting on its taken argument's cause at Calls.cs:391 (h2 never reaches selection); a shared join-rests
    completion for DecideResult (it changed no probe).

- **BU-79 Rule W: a failed part is a wildcard; only a node's own verdict over a failed child is suppressed** (2026-11-02, the owner's
  「了解しました。5件とも推奨どおり進めてください。」; the done-when, DECISIONS Q13) Supersedes BU-77 (FailedFit, its readers C15 and C16, B1, B2, and step 1's
  certain rule) and BU-78's B4 and fix (a).
  - The reason that no longer holds: those readers tried to decide exactly which records a failed part makes dependent. That cannot
    be decided locally (evidence-fixed slots, clause-only slots, pairings), and SPEC 23.1.2 does not require it: an implementation
    may report a dependent failure, and must not lose an independent one.
  - The rule (ArgumentKinds' contract): a failed part fits every candidate and is no evidence (U1.6d). Only a node's own verdict over
    a failed child is suppressed: a join's DecideRest, BU-78's sites 2-4, and CompleteJoinResults. Every other record of the call is
    reported: Ambiguous, UnboundTypeArgument, NoApplicable, and an unselected call's part records; beside an unbound failed argument,
    only the checks SPEC 10.1 makes before inference (the G455 amendment below).
  - An unselected call's held join that its formation judged Conflict still writes its own record (ReportHeldConflicts, the part of
    BU-78's fix (a) that reports, not rests). Without it, an independent TypeMismatch_Kd would be lost (ACRT a1 and a3, f1).
  - Deleted: Binding.ArgumentKinds.FailedFits.cs (FailedFit, its scope, PublishFailedFit, PublishHeldFailures, RestingFailedPart,
    AmbiguityRestingPart, CertainMismatch); PublishJudged, RestJudged, RestOnVerdict, HasOwnCause and FailJudged; IsOwnLength.
  - The done-when (Q13): only an acceptance move, an InternalInvariant_Kd or Language error on a valid program, or a lost independent
    record blocks; dependent records added or removed are counted by class.
  - Amended (G455, 2026-11-06; unit bu190): a named, method, constructor, requirement or constraint-based value call with an
    unprepared argument (an unbound failed part; BindCallCore, SelectValueCall) runs only the checks SPEC 10.1 makes before inference,
    which read no argument's Type, and reports their records: the group's acquisition-shape contracts (the 10.1 preamble, 7.4.4), the
    explicit Type arguments' own records, and NoApplicableOverload_Kd when no candidate passes step 1 (the count and kinds of the
    explicit Type arguments, `ExplicitTypeArgumentsFit`, which TryCandidateCore reads too) and step 2 (argument matching:
    `MapCallArguments`; `MapValueCallArguments` for a constraint-based value call, which passes every argument positionally, 10.1.1).
    That NoApplicable holds under every repair of the part. Every other outcome rests on the part, as before, in either argument order
    at named and constraint-based value calls alike. FitArgument keeps its rule-W row for a part that kept its Type (U2.1 r2-3).
    Records added, each independent: NoApplicableOverload_Kd (arity, a label, the `!` boundary, a default, an excess argument, the
    explicit Type arguments' count or kind), UnprovenAcquisitionCorrelation_Kd (7.4.4's call contract) and an explicit Type argument's
    own UnresolvedBinding_Kd. Step 1 judges every kind before a failed Type argument rests, so a call with no unprepared argument
    reports a later kind misfit too (`pair<Undefined, 3>(5)`, as `pair<3, Undefined>(5)` already did). Not covered (PLAN G500): the checks after step 2 beside the part (another argument's or the result's
    misfit, Ambiguous, UnboundTypeArgument, an arity misfit beside a failed explicit Type argument, the selected candidate's own
    records), and a plain value call (BindValueCall), whose count and label checks are the base's other copy of 10.1.1's value-call
    rule; G494's unit 2 replaces them with `MapValueCallArguments` judged up front. Rejected: judging every candidate with the part a
    wildcard (option A): later checks read the missing evidence as a rejection (until PLAN G463, `ConstructorType`'s construction-target Origin), and an
    Unsupported part's dependent UnboundTypeArgument_Kd is a Language error on a valid program (Milestone 41).

- **BU-81 HIR publication is eager at the end of each Final pass; R7 writes inline** (2026-11-02; R6-check H1a, behavior-preserving;
  the owner's Q8 approval 「Q8を承認」, R5-M23, design `draft/Sketches/R5 Step 0/Q8-design-2.md` D9 and `Q8-package.md` §3.7; H0's
  division, R5-M182) Refines R2b-D2 ("lazily, at most once per Binding pass").
  - `Binding.Check` (`Binding.Check.cs`) is three steps: the failure producers (the Final prologue: definition obligations,
    specification links, needed conformance paths and capability sites, derived uses; per node: a failed called declaration, the
    call and runtime-test Constraint checks, the part prerequisites, Unvisited to Unresolved; then the sites the loop's checks needed),
    in a Final pass the publication of every module with the library (`PublishPass`), then the counting of states and issues.
    `CheckBound` runs the same steps. `PublishHir()` after a Final pass returns its version without work; after another pass it
    publishes once, as before.
  - The reason that no longer holds: lazy publication kept Bind-only callers from paying for the columns, but H1 judges the published
    columns inside the Final pass before the counting (Q8 D8). After G2 every Analyze publishes anyway, so production pays nothing new;
    Bind-only callers (tests, hover without analysis) pay one publication per Final pass.
  - `PublishSites` is deleted: its failure of the loop's needed sites is `FailNeededSites` after the loop, and the counting records
    and counts each such Use once, as it does the prologue's.
  - Superseded in part by R7-M7: the HIR publisher walk stays a lasting component.
- **BU-83 Rule E: an erasure is its node's only implicit adaptation** (2026-11-03; PLAN G341, scheduled by the owner after G216 (a)'s
  joint landing, 「合同着地が完了したら、下記のOpen issuesに着手してください。」)
  - The defect: a value call (U1) or a Case payload (U2) that received a stored Copy Closure at a Function parameter was
    `TransferRequired_Kd`, while the named call was valid. Two consumers judged the source's acquisition again on the erased Function
    Type, which is Non-Copy (SPEC 7.7.4), where SPEC 3.5 and 7.7.4 judge it on the source's own Type.
  - The rule (SPEC 7.7.4, 3.5, 10.2, 12.5.2): when Binding has erased a source at its position (`ErasedFunctionType`), `AdaptInput`
    (Binding.ArgumentOperations), the one function value-call arguments and payloads pass through, reports the erased Type with quality
    Erasure. An erased payload involves two acquisitions (SPEC 7.7.4: erasure acquires its source ordinarily and is an owning
    conversion, distinct from a Copy or Move of the source):
    - (i) the source's: `AdaptInput`'s rule-E row judges its bare acquisition once, on its own Type, through `AcquiresBare`, the
      by-value row's predicate (one rule for both rows); a Move fails with `TransferRequired_Kd` at the source (`RequireAcquisition`,
      `FailAcquisition`), at value calls and payloads alike. It is published once, as the source's Adjust (`ChildAdjust`, `BareOf`;
      R4-M142), which MIR reads, as at a named call;
    - (ii) the erased value's: a fresh temporary, so a payload slot takes it by Move (`plan.SetAcquisition`), unchanged.
  - One representation: `ArgumentType` presents an erased source's own Type, as it does a referent read, so an Erasure operation's
    `SourceType` is the source's own Type at both sites. The structural fit stays on the erased Type (rejected (b)).
  - A payload (U2): `Binding.Enums` adapts the source's completed Type, without its own copy of the erasure; `CompleteEnumAcquisitions`'
    bare row reads `SourceType` and never sees a Move of an erased source, which `AdaptInput` failed first. It fails the construction
    at the source, as `AdaptInput`'s acquisition failure does, so no resolved construction keeps an invalid plan (that was a broken HIR
    contract, `InternalInvariant_Kd`).
  - A Non-Copy erased source keeps its record, Binding's `TransferRequired_Kd` at the source, at both sites, beside any independent
    record and once per use (the value call's record had been the old Analysis's alone, lost beside another Binding error).
  - The old Analysis (U4; R5's consent with conditions, 2026-11-03): its erased branch (`OwnershipAnalysis.Expression`) forwarded a
    payload's committed acquisition, (ii), to the source as well, so a payload Moved a stored Copy Closure (`MovedPlace_Kd`). It now
    passes none: the source is acquired by its bare acquisition, and `Argument` checks the committed acquisition against the erasure's
    temporary. The line goes with the old Analysis at H10b (R5-M182's amendment). Acceptance moves (Q13, named): p_useafter_ok,
    p_useafter2_ok, p_twice_ok, p_then_v_ok and p_gen_useafter_ok become valid; p_twice_nc stays rejected on both pipelines.
  - Rejected: (a) skipping `AdaptInput` for an erased value-call part, a clause for one form that leaves payloads broken; (b) fitting
    the source's own Type structurally, which the check refuses (Closure against Function: `NoApplicableOverload_Kd`); (c) waiting for
    H1, which never sees a call Binding failed; (d) leaving the value call's Non-Copy record to the old Analysis.
  - Applied to the Adjust column by G386 (2026-11-05): the ErasedType column alone says where an erasure is applied, at the node Binding
    erased (`ChildAdjust`, a group's operand); a value operation's Erasure is only the selection's quality, so `HirAdjust.Of` gives it
    no adaptation, and a parenthesized callable argument is erased once.

- **BU-82 The Semantics-case renderer is one Binding component** (2026-11-03; R6-check Q8-6, behavior-preserving; the owner's Q8
  approval 「Q8を承認」 with proposal Q8-6, R5-M23; H0's division, R5-M182)
  - Responsibility: `Binding.Diagnostics.Cases` renders Semantics cases in a record and is their one renderer: a binder's name and
    found Semantics (`s = ref or uniq`); a case set as the `case` fact (`CaseFact`: per binder when it is a product, a binder found
    under all its admitted cases omitted, else the list of cases); the `case` evidence; the Note `Found under the Semantics case ...
    (SPEC 8.15)`; the related declarations of the named bindings; and the explicit-entry Note tail (`FailingCaseNote`).
  - Inputs: a definition's pair binders and a set of case bits in their enumeration order (the innermost resolved binder advancing
    fastest, each in `SemanticsMask` order, the numbering of the old Analysis' `BuildCases` and of `MirCases`' views), or a failing
    mask. Outputs: text, evidence and related declarations. It decides no case and reads no analysis; it runs only for a published
    record.
  - Callers: Binding's capture-entry record (`FailingCaseNote`) and the old Analysis' case records, which call it until H10b deletes
    that Analysis (R5-M182's amendment of Q8's "until H11"). H3-2's MIR views give their `case:Text` through it (H0a §4.1).
  - BU-44's `OriginDiagnostics.CaseText` names its binders through `BinderName` but keeps its own list: it joins the cases of one
    class requirement, `, ` where every binder must give the class (a product) and `; ` where one suffices (a union), which is not a
    found case set.

- **BU-85 Binding judges its obligations at Final; no obligation reaches Analysis unjudged** (2026-11-03; R6-check H1b, H0b-13 of
  `draft/Sketches/R6-check/H0b-flip.md`, BU's answer BU-5; H0's division, R5-M182)
  - The reason is H1b's census. Over the test suite, the corpus, the library and the harnessed milestones, no obligation reached the
    old non-relation branch (`UnprovenConstraint_Kd`) under complete Binding.
  - `Binding.Obligations` owns the obligations: their record (`AddObligation`), the length verification and the Final pass's
    verdict (`JudgeObligations`, today the Definition obligations' `FailTypeRole`). Its entry file states the contract.
  - H1b-1 (behavior-preserving) deletes `BindingObligationKind.Loan` and `StaticStorage`: no rule produced either, so they were
    unreachable by construction.
  - H1b-2: a symbolic length is proven where it is formed (`Binding.Lengths` `BindLength`, SPEC 4.4.1, 4.4.2), with or without a
    Function scope. Before, a length outside a Function scope (only under a misplaced length list, `struct S<length N>`) became an
    unproven obligation that only the old Analysis' non-relation branch could see. It now fails at the length with the site's
    existing code, `InvalidTypeFormation` (`InvalidTypeFormation_Kd`). Such a program already carries the Parse error
    `MisplacedSyntax_Kd`, so the record is a dependent one added on a rejected program (Q13). The Final check can then never fire
    on a parse-error program.
  - H1b-3: `JudgeObligations` checks the contract. Every obligation other than a Definition obligation and an Origin relation with
    both ends is judged by Final:
    - a length is proven where it forms (H1b-2);
    - an `OriginInference` is discharged when its local's Type and initializer bind (`ResolveInitializerOrigins`,
      `InferLocalOrigins`);
    - no other form is produced.

    One left over bound parts fails its use with `Internal` (`InternalInvariant_Kd`). One over a failed part rests on that failure
    (rule W, BU-79): the census found all 30 such programs failing at the local's initializer. The old reporter's non-relation
    branch becomes the same contract (`OwnershipRequirement.Internal`). `UnprovenOrigin` then always names a relation, so
    `OwnershipIssue.Code` gives it 2 codes, and ledger row :51 is dropped (R4-M112's amendment).

- **BU-86 A Pending candidate's judgment before its proof is one fact** (2026-11-03; PLAN G354 (1), scheduled by the owner after the
  joint landing, 「合同着地が完了したら、下記のOpen issuesに着手してください。」)
  - The defect: a judgment that left a candidate Pending before its proof published no fact, so the call ended in a fact-less
    `UnprovenConstraint_Kd` (`FailWaitingSelection`). The census reached L184, L488 and L531(b) of `TryCandidateCore`.
  - The fact: `PendingJudgment` (`Binding.CandidateEvaluation`), a closed vocabulary, written once where `TryCandidateCore` decides
    and kept as the trial's fact (`trialPending`, the trial frame's row beside `trialClause`). Transport: the proof channel's trial
    frame (r2-6); `CloseTrial` hands it to the selection's frame. Its consumer, the candidate's selection (`EvaluateCallCandidate`),
    takes it once per Pending candidate (`TakeTrialPending`) under the channel's consumer rule (`OwnFrame`, shared by every consumer
    of a carried fact): no fact is normal, a stamp other than the innermost open frame's is `InternalInvariant_Kd`.
  - `FailedTypeArgument` (L184): an explicit Type argument that did not bind. Writer: the explicit-argument loop. Reader:
    `EvaluateCallCandidate`, which rests the selection on it (`FailedPendingSignature`, then `CompleteDependent`), as on a failed
    parameter Type (SPEC 23.1.2). The call adds no record of its own (`g<Undefined>(1)`: the argument's `UnresolvedBinding_Kd` only).
  - `EnvironmentResult` (L488, L531(b)): an argument whose known signature's result over its closure's environment is no evidence
    for a slot (SPEC 8.10, 7.7.4) that no other evidence binds (amended 2026-11-03, below). Writer: `Infer` (`Binding.CallSlots`),
    where it judges that result, records the judgment per slot (`environmentJudgments`, the argument and the slot); the trial
    publishes one as its fact (`EnvironmentJudgment`, below) at the two Pending returns it decides (`PendingOnEnvironment`): L488,
    and L531's result without a Type; L531's unsubstituted Origin publishes none. Reader: the Unproven branch (`Binding.Calls`), for
    a single Pending candidate after
    the Callable and Constraint facts, as it reads `ConstraintFailure` (`FailPendingJudgment`). The record keeps
    `UnprovenConstraint_Kd` at the call; the adapter (`ReportPendingJudgment`) adds the argument as related location `argument`
    and the Note "The result of c over its environment is no evidence for T".
  - Not columns: L418, L443 and L531(a) (length forms, revision B and G216 (a) step 2); L153, L314, L374 and FitArgument (not
    reached); L593 (G354 (2)).
  - Amended 2026-11-03 (G354-1c; kept with BU by the owner, PLAN G354). The trial's one first-written judgment counted even when
    another evidence bound its slot, so a Pending return named a judgment that did not decide. Now `Infer` records the judgment per
    slot, and after `UnsolvedSlots`, with every piece of evidence in (arguments, call signatures, the expected result, SolveLate),
    `EnvironmentJudgment` publishes that of the first unsolved slot in slot order, never by argument order (SPEC 10.8: traversal order
    never chooses a solution), and none when every such slot is bound; a bound slot's part is judged by the Callable proof or the
    conversion (SPEC 10.8: only parts containing an unbound slot are matched; SPEC 8.10). Named acceptance class: a candidate whose
    environment slot another evidence binds, including the expected result, is refuted by its Callable Constraint, so another candidate
    that applies is selected (`make(c@ref, n, 2)` beside `make<F>(f: ref/F, t: i32, u: i64)`; `let r: i32 = make(c@ref, 2)` beside
    `make<F>(f: ref/F, u: i64)`). A Literal at T is no evidence (SPEC 10.2.1), so `make(c@ref, 1)` keeps the fact. Open: an environment
    judgment on an unsolved slot still makes the candidate Pending before an independent Constraint's refutation. L531's
    unsubstituted-Origin return stays fact-less: valid programs reach it.

  - The defect: position waiting (AwaitsFor, SPEC 14.9.2 step 3) re-walked every Waiting join a source held, down to its leaves,
    at each question, so it grew as program size × nesting depth on nested joins (V16).
  - Owner: ResultPropagation. The fact is a per-pass column beside the outcome on the pooled `ResultContext`, reset by `Clear` at each
    rent. Its one writer is `ResultContext.Wait(awaiting)`, the one writer of `JoinOutcome.Waiting`: both Waiting sites
    (`AwaitsWithoutCandidate`, `DecideResult`'s `ConflictWaits`) publish `SourcesAwait` once, when the join's sources are reached and
    each held join's own fact is published. When a call takes a waiting argument's parts (`TakeWaiting`) and decides it again
    (`DecideTaken`), `PublishAwaiting` republishes the argument's held Waiting joins innermost first, over the held-part walk
    (`AddHeldParts`, G368 (3)) and each held join's waited sources, in JudgeHeld's order. Two windows take or bind parts without
    republication: a Case construction's TakeWaiting (`Binding.Enums`) or a failing CompleteWaiting, and an enclosing root's step 3
    before the held join's DecideWaiting; no reader of the fact was found there.
  - Readers: `AwaitsFor`'s result-target row (a Waiting join answers with the fact; every AwaitsFor and AwaitsPosition caller reads
    it) and `BoundSince` (Deferred). BoundSince's Waiting row is a decision, not a consequence of the sources: a Waiting join is
    bound since by its outcome, whatever its sources hold since. Its effect after TakeWaiting: a held Waiting join one of whose
    sources holds a failed Tuple element beside a function its call completed is now Deferred, where the deleted walk made it not
    Deferred and its root rested on the cause without judging the tree. Its root now judges it (JudgeHeld), so the join's own
    conflict among the completed functions is reported, an independent record (SPEC 23.1.2) the walk had lost.
  - Removed: the re-walk of held Waiting joins and `BoundSince`'s walk over a Waiting join's waited sources (G335's "Completed").
    No removal condition: the fact is canonical. AwaitsFor's other rows (literal parts, AwaitsCall, an Unvisited literal) stay
    structural per-node answers; a column for them would be a second representation.

    A part the call cannot take (a failed preparation or completion, a failed waiting part, a structural misfit, a failed fit) takes

- **BU-103 A failed acquisition is `HirAcquire.Failed`** (2026-11-05; superseded in part by BU-110; PLAN G422, unit bu149; design
  revision 2, design review 1 REVISE, its re-check ACCEPT; the owner approved the entry beyond `HirAcquire`'s limit 7, verbatim

    was never written (`=> t.5`; `=> b` of a Type whose Copy proof is Error; `else => x` left `y` unwritten, and A1 reported
    `UninitializedPlace_Kd`), and `Derived` (`!= default`) never folded an Error node's failed acquisition.
  - Rule: `HirAcquire.Failed` has one meaning: a consumed Place or a Pattern binding whose acquisition failed (no Type, a failed Pattern

    `BareOf` and in `HirAdjust.Of(PatternAcquisition)` (`None or Deferred`), one row each, with no default; `Unset` means only that no
    consumer takes the node. An Error node's Failed folds to `(Temporary, None)` (R4-M109 Rule 2); a discarded failed Place's plan row
    is Failed. `MirBuilder.Operand` derives Failed with no record; an `Unset` Adjust reaching it is a broken HIR contract,

    derived value of a Place Binding failed" and "a trailing item whose column is unset so reaches the same case": a failed row or

    `MirBuildTest.AFailedDiscardRowIsDerivedFromABindingError`).
  - Records (Q13): dependent `UninitializedPlace_Kd` removals at a Var whose branch value was a failed Place (rule W); no acceptance
    moves.
  - Rejected: `(Temporary, None)` for a failed Place (above); a row in `MirBuilder.Acquired` (Failed never reaches it).

    default) `WellFormedPart` stops at a slot of the pattern: the slot's solution is its contributor's (the expected result or a

    so a method's declaring-Type slot is no stop and a constructor keeps its slots), a payload's declared Type, a property update's
    operation Type; `Type` its instantiation (null: no bound). `Contribute` runs in `SolveLate` after the late evidence pass, so a
    root row's Type is the instantiation today's collection read.

    (`CollectPositionPremises`, Rows.cs), the rows `JudgePositionRows` judges; the per-parameter whole-Type collection goes. A trial's
    composition may stop early where the literal's shape does not fit (the fit rejects the candidate); the judgment's fails Internal
    there, after judging the rows before it (U1's N1 order).

    names and no evidence position's pattern names (an Evidence root row's or the receiver's; `MentionsOriginSlot`, shared with
    `OpenResultOnlyOrigins`), and publishes them as `OriginInference.PremiseSolved` (one writer, `DiscoverPremiseOrigins`); the

BU-95's set demand (`Binding.Types.cs`) is an ordinary demand inside its suspended consultation frame; its

- **BU-104 A candidate's position rows are composed once, at its first solve, and every later reading reads them** (2026-11-05;

  - R3: a candidate's child rows are composed once, at its first `SolveLate` (`RetainChildRows`, the probe's state: a waiting join,

    construction's, a value call's and a fixed construction's re-check their own). Every later reading reads the slice and composes
    nothing: a later solve of the candidate (the re-run after `CompleteWaiting`, `CheckDefaulted`'s) instantiates each leaf's `Pattern`
    under its own solution; the judgment (`JudgePositionRows`) derives Types top-down from the operation's Type by the new `Index`
    column. A retained row holds structure (`Argument`, `Parent` relative to its slice, `Index`, `Part`), `Pattern` and
    `Contribution`; `Type` is the reading's; a part's failure is read at the reading (rule W). `childRows` is one list whose
    evaluations append and remove their own rows when they end (nested evaluations end first), so a warm Bind allocates nothing.
    Supersedes BU-94's "child rows ... removed when the argument's judgment ends"; BU-94 and BU-99 stay.
  - R3': an independently typed control-flow part (a join the call does not classify, its own formation's Type) is one position and

  - R4/R4': an argument whose root has child rows is judged by its rows wherever a root is read (named calls in `JudgeSelectedCall`,
    value calls, Case constructions), whether or not its operation adapted it; no aggregate of the leaves is formed. A root's
    Contribution is read only for a root without child rows; `EvidenceNames` reads the Evidence leaf rows, the Evidence roots without
    child rows and the receiver, never a composed root's mark. `PartContribution`'s Join row reads "a control-flow part is Evidence".
  - Evidence of the cause (the front's step 0, on dev ae112e08f): a join argument took `JudgeSelectedCall`'s rows branch, whose second
    composition read completion state and found no child rows, so the root was judged as one Evidence leaf; each form had one solve,
    whose `PremiseSolved` was empty because `EvidenceNames` read the join root's Evidence mark.
  - Not in U3a: composition beneath a slot (R5, U3b); the Join record as a waiting fact, the survey path and one formation (U6).
  - Twelfth amendment (2026-11-06; U3-design.md's twelfth amendment, C-49 and its re-check ACCEPT; the owner, verbatim 「Dは放棄します。
    U3aについては、もう一度だけ設計して下さい。」 and 「B1 を直す」). Supersedes BU-51's region clause.
    - Call regions (SPEC 15.6.4 step 1): after each candidate's solve, and at a function reference, a callee Origin that 15.3.6 leaves
      without a candidate is a region of the executable body the call lies in, one per call and Origin (`OpenUnsolvedOrigins`,
      replacing `OpenResultOnlyOrigins` and its result-only guard). Every relation of the call over it is a body row

    - A5's meet law at a shorter end (SPEC 15.3.6), the last step of `ClassEdges`, read by Judge and by Outlives: for a non-Fixed meet
      and each in-edge whose tail is not an operand, an edge to the canonical meet of each choice of one bound per operand, at the
      in-edge's site and row, judged as any edge into a Fixed node. An operand's bounds are the operand when Fixed, else each Fixed
      node its walk meets and each bound of a meet it enters; the walk stops at Fixed nodes and never follows an operand's edge into
      its own meet (`o outlives (o and ...)` bounds nothing). `TyCtxt.MeetAtom` (the view's `Meet` and `InternAtom`) gives the
      canonical meet, Fixed, its part the operands' union.

      (`OriginAtomEntry.EnclosingCallRegion`, set at `ClassifyAtom`'s row 6 and carried by a meet from an operand). A5 reads it at

      body is G216 (b)'s.

      the judgment about a callee Parameter atom the call had left in the caller.
  - Amended (G410, 2026-11-06; SPEC 3.8, 10.8, 15.3.6, 15.6.4 step 1): a callee's Input Origin (one a parameter's layer elides, which
    `during x` names) that 15.3.6 leaves without a candidate, as after a Never argument, which fits and supplies no Origin, or an
    omitted default, which is no evidence, is a region of its call like an Origin parameter. `OpenUnsolvedOrigins` opens both: the
    parameters keyed up from `UnsolvedKey`, the inputs down (`UnsolvedKey - 1 - i`), all below `UnsolvedKey / 2`, so `IsCallRegion`

- **BU-102 The C1-F4 view is its own validator: a broken contract throws in a complete compilation** (2026-11-05; PLAN G423, G263's
  item 3: R4's recommendation (c), accepted in G263's review N5; R4's consent C-20 for the MIR lines; supersedes in part R4-M101 E2 and

  - Rule: the view's producer (`Binding.OriginRows.cs`, `.Atoms.cs`) checks its contract where it forms a row or an atom. In a complete
    compilation a break throws at its site (`BrokenContract`) and ends the check as `CheckFaulted_Kd`, as `Binding.Readable` does
    (BU-36). The walk's version, a slice's index and an atom are stored only after their checks pass, and the part check runs at every
    read, so every later read throws again. In an incomplete compilation the state rests on a Binding failure, and the view keeps it.
  - The contract, each condition by construction but for the unverified cases below: no row with no body is left (the declaration
    judge consumes every one whose ends are declaration atoms, BU-26, BU-89, and a header names no other: a body stamps each
    non-declaration atom, R4-M101 E1); a case binder is its body's (only a declaration's scope declares a pair binder); every atom has a
    class and none is Dependent (E1; only a Binding failure leaves an Unbound or pending atom, R4-M118); a unit names a non-Fixed atom of
    its own part or of none.
  - Unverified (R4-M118's two cases, carried forward by PLAN G440): an Unbound atom left by path d (`PendingAssociatedType`'s early
    return) or at a use outside its owner's subtree that `OriginAtUse` cannot resolve. R4-M118's guard (F) closed them; this throw now
    does. Showing that a later bind completes every Type that return leaves or an Error rests on it, and that no row or atom names an
    Unbound atom outside its owner's subtree, verifies them.
  - Part rule (E4, one form on both paths): an atom's part is its forming unit's (`PartOf`: 1 the constructor's body, 2 its layer, a
    meet its operands'), as R4-M114 gave an atom MIR reads; a declaration atom or another body's belongs to no part. Rows gave every end
    their row's part, so a callee's Unclassed Parameter atoms (PLAN G195) named by both parts reached both: dev's finding, the first
    commit's throw (review 1's B-1). Unclassed atoms form no edge, so no oracle choice reads their part.
  - Reason: the view is built after Bind, on MIR's first read, when Binding's records are final, and atoms are also read at MIR sites.
  - Removes: `TyCtxt.OriginFindings`, Binding's list and `OriginFinding`, and the `InternalInvariant_Kd` loop of `MirOrigins.Findings`.
    `Findings` keeps G215's layer limit (R4-M168).
  - Rejected: `InternalInvariant_Kd` at the site. A record after Bind needs the removed channel, or an eager build at Bind's end that
    cannot cover `OriginAtomIn`'s MIR-site atoms, which makes two mechanisms. Also rejected: keeping the list for a later reader, and
    exempting Unclassed atoms from E4's check (a second form of the part rule).

- **BU-107 An erasure's failed Owned part is the converted value's own failure; before the capability engine judges, it is the
