  - Amended by R5-M176 (PLAN G364): `Kotonoha`, the owner of the names, also owns the logical declaration order (SPEC 6.2.1) they
    define, through `Kotonoha.AddSources`; `TestCatalog` no longer sorts a module's documents itself.
- **R5-M176 One owner of the logical declaration order: `Kotonoha.AddSources` (PLAN G364)** (2026-11-02, the owner's 「G364から始めて」; amends
  R5-M175) SPEC 6.2.1 orders declarations from different SourceDocuments by the documents' logical names as UTF-8 byte sequences, then by
  position; Field initializers run in that order and Fields are destroyed in reverse (SPEC 6.2, 16.3.2), so the order is observable. The
  compiler's order was its parse order: `Project` parsed product sources as `GetFiles` listed them (UTF-16 ordinal full paths),
  TestSources after them and `Project.AddSource`'s in-memory documents last, and `TestCatalog` re-sorted a module's documents under UTF-16
  ordinal for the artifact identity, a second copy of an order.
  - Rule: `Kotonoha`, which owns the logical names (R5-M175), owns their order. `Kotonoha.AddSources(IReadOnlyList<SourceDocument>)`
    records and parses one call's documents in a stable sort by `LogicalName` under `UnicodeNameHelper.ScalarOrder` (equal names, which
    `CheckNames` reports, keep their given order), after every earlier call's documents; `AddSource(document)` is its one-document form.
    `SourceDocuments` is in this order. A producer adds a module's ordinary sources in one call, so generated fragments
    (`CodeContext.Parse`, recorded later) follow them all.
  - Comparer: `UnicodeNameHelper.ScalarOrder`, UTF-8 byte order (Unicode scalar order) computed on UTF-16 without encoding: at the first
    differing code unit surrogates rank above U+E000–U+FFFF, and a proper prefix comes first; a lone surrogate (a name `CheckNames`
    rejects) orders by its code unit, so the order stays total. No allocation.
  - Producer: `Project.CheckFrontEnd` collects each module's ordinary documents (product, TestSources and in-memory ones) and gives each
    module one `AddSources` call, in `SourceModules` order. Reads, read failures and `Diagnostics.AddInput` stay at read time in command
    order (SPEC 23.2.2), so the diagnostic source table keeps consumption order; parsing still precedes the established check, so a read
    failure still reports the other documents' syntax errors (SPEC 23.1.2). In-memory documents now join the root's call before that
    check, so a failed read also reports their own syntax errors.
  - Consumers: `TestCatalog` reads `SourceDocuments` in its order (its sort is removed); the artifact identity changes only for a module
    whose names UTF-16 and UTF-8 order differently. Documentation orders a declaration's fragments in SPEC 6.2.1's shape (ordinary
    before generated, then `ModId ?? LogicalName`, the addition order, the position), in `Binding.GetDocumentation` and hover's
    documentation (`HoverBuilder`, after its project key, which stays ordinal); its name key now compares with `ScalarOrder` instead
    of `string.CompareOrdinal`.
  - Kept: the multi-key record orders of IMPL 20.6.4 (the test listing and results by name, logical source path and project identity:
    `TestCatalog.Compare`, `TestCommand`'s outcome sort, and the sites' order that numbers SiteIds) keep `string.CompareOrdinal`. They
    order test records under the test protocol's contract, not declarations under SPEC 6.2.1; a similar shape under another contract
    stays separate (AGENTS, Share by meaning).
  - Out of scope, unchanged: the Kimi library's hand order (`KimiLibrarySources`; no library struct's Fields span documents: no
    container is declared in two library documents, and signature documents add only functions); Mod-generated fragments and
    `CodeContext.Parse` (an API, call order); `DependencyResolver`'s, `CheckInputSource`'s and `DiskReader`'s listing orders, which
    now decide read order only. SPEC 23.2.3's unit order (Unicode scalar order of the selected paths) is not implemented: JSON
    `kimi check` takes one input (STATUS's conformance note: single-unit `kimi.check/2`); when it is built, it uses `ScalarOrder`.
  - Rejected: a sort in `Project` (the order would have a second owner beside the names' owner, and `TestCatalog` kept its own copy);
    sorting the reads (reads and their failures are consumed in command order, SPEC 23.2.2); `StringComparer.Ordinal` (UTF-16 order,
    wrong where a supplementary scalar meets U+E000–U+FFFF).
- **R5-M177 One owner of the configuration rules, the TestSources rule included; each failure its own record (PLAN G367)** (2026-11-02,
  the owner's list 「現状出来る作業（G367、G359、G357、G363、G366、U11など）を、順に行ってください。」) SPEC 23.1.2 reports each independent failed requirement.
  `DependencyConfiguration.Validate` and `NativeConfiguration.Validate` returned the first failure, so a load, a preparation and
  `Compilation.Prepare` each reported one; the duplicate-TestSources rule (IMPL 20.1: entries compared as resolved paths) had three copies
  stopping at the first duplicate (`Project.BuildTargets`, `PrepareTests`, `DependencyResolver.Load`) and a fourth, ordinal one in
  `Validate`.
  - Rule: `DependencyConfiguration` owns every configuration rule. `Validate(ProjectFile)` (directory-free: the load and
    `Compilation.Prepare`) and `Validate(ProjectFile, directory, out testSources)` (the same plus the TestSources compared as resolved
    paths, and the resolved set: product and test preparation, the resolver) return one note per independent failure, empty and
    allocation-free when valid. Independent: KotonohaArray, the identity, each reference's name, identity and source, each native
    target, entry and requirement, each Alias and PackageSources entry, each TestSources entry's syntax and each duplicate. Left out
    as dependent: the checks that read a null map, a null native target's entries, the other checks of a null native entry or of a
    packaged record without a valid Name, a merge pair with an invalid packaged record, a null reference's source, and comparing an
    entry that breaks the path syntax (one predicate, `ValidTestSource`).
  - Shape: a list of notes, as `Kotonoha.CheckNames` (R5-M175), each its own record of the existing code: `ProjectPreparationFailed_Kd`
    through `Project.Fail` (test preparation now reports its configuration failures through its owner and publishes them for the
    command, as the product does, instead of throwing one `InvalidDataException`), `InvalidDependencyConfiguration_Kd`
    (`Compilation.Prepare`), `ProjectLoadFailed_Kd` (`ProjectFile.Load` throws `ProjectConfigurationException` carrying the notes;
    `Project.TryCreate`'s `failures`, `LoadedProject.Failures`, `CheckOutput.Blocked(notes)`, one solution-load line each). Equal notes
    merge in `DiagnosticOwner`, a grouping SPEC 23.1.2 leaves to the implementation. No code is added and no note text changes.
  - Deleted: the three resolved copies and the ordinal one (a TestSources entry spelled twice now loads and is reported at preparation
    with every other duplicate); `PrepareTests`' own base directory (`Path.GetFullPath(Directory)`, which threw for a project without
    one; the product form, the current directory, now serves both).
  - Resolver (G367b): `DependencyPartition` carries `ResolutionFailure[] Failures` (a `(Code, Message)` record; null when resolved)
    instead of one `ReasonCode` and `Diagnostic`, and the resolver records each independent failure instead of throwing at the first:
    each failed reference (UnsupportedPackage, IdentityMismatch, the root Cycle, NotLibrary, ConflictingInput, ReferenceReassignment,
    each invalid test reference) adds no edge, and a node that fails to load (I/O, each configuration note, a duplicate TestSources)
    adds no children, so their dependents are left out (a failed load is remembered, so a project several references reach fails
    once); TargetMismatch and LanguageMismatch are recorded and the node still resolves; without the root or its target nothing else
    resolves; acyclicity is checked over the resolved part. A lock records the first
    failure's code (`reasonCode`, schema unchanged); `DependencyLock.Validate` gives every failure, each a `ProjectPreparationFailed_Kd`
    through `Project.Fail` (test preparation too, no longer one `InvalidDataException`), and `kimi restore` prints each.
    `DuplicateTestSource` becomes `InvalidConfiguration` (the configuration's owner reports it). A dependency's directory-free failures,
    found by `ProjectFile.Load`, still hide its TestSources comparison until fixed (the load precedes the comparison, as for a root).
  - Input validators (G367c, the same cause one level higher): `Compilation.Prepare` records the configuration, the unresolved graph,
    the language version, the target and each compile-time setting independently: the settings are checked against the fixed Condition
    names (`Compilation.Conditions`, the one table the Conditions are built from), so an unsupported target leaves out only its
    Conditions. `PrepareModules` records each dependency setting and, through
    `NativeConfiguration.ValidateGraphSupplies` (replacing `ValidatePackageSupplies` and `ValidateSupplyAgreement`), each requirement a
    supply for a resolved module breaks (a missing ContractId and a different Sha256 independently) and each conflicting merge, at its
    module. `TestSettings.Validate` returns its notes (each deadline, the budgets, each environment entry), and test preparation
    records them with the test identity (`TestCatalog.TryProjectIdOf`) instead of throwing; the command's merged options still throw
    their first (a command option error, not an Input record). `ProjectFile.Load` collects each repeated or invalid setting
    (`ValidateMapNames`) into its `ProjectConfigurationException`; a rule that reads a repeated or ambiguous map (Dependencies,
    NativeRequirements, NativeLibraries) reads it as empty, and every other configuration rule still reports. The packaged-record merge
    compares a pair only when both are valid, without a per-target array, so validation stays allocation-free when valid.
    Kept: a Tinyhand syntax failure stays one `TinyhandException`; a test target that cannot be selected stays a throw.
  - Rejected: validating the configuration only at preparation (the language server's project item reads the maps after the load); a
    mode flag or an optional directory steering one `Validate`; joining the notes into one record's text.
- **R5-M178 The built-in Conditions `os` and `arch` by IMPL 20.2.1's table: `TargetTriple.OsFamily` and `ArchFamily` (PLAN G370)**
  (2026-11-02, G363's review) Major.
  - Cause: `Compilation.Prepare` derived `os` from LLVM's OS classification (`OsType`: two switch arms, any other OS its enum name)
    and `arch` from the `Architecture` enum's name, so `darwin` gave `darwin`, `freebsd13.2` `freebsd`, `armv7` `arm` and `x86_64h`
    `x86_64`, where IMPL 20.2.1 gives `macos`, `unknown`, `unknown` and `unknown`.
  - Rule: `TargetTriple` publishes `OsFamily` and `ArchFamily` from one table of IMPL 20.2.1's rows, a row per spelling: the OS
    component without its version suffix (digits and dots) and the architecture component exactly; any other spelling, or no OS
    component, is `unknown`. `Compilation.Prepare` reads them; `windows`, `linux` and `macos` stay `os == ...` (SPEC 19.2.1). A new
    spelling adds a row. Windows triples keep their values.
  - Replaces: Compilation's switch and enum-name lowering, and `TargetTriple.Os` with LLVM's OS parse (`ParseOs`) and `OsType`, whose
    one reader was that switch. `Arch` (LLVM's architecture with its aliases) stays for the pointer width (R5-M174): another contract.
  - IMPL's `x86` row is unreachable: the LLVM architecture parse does not know `x86`, so an `x86-...` triple has no IR target
    (`UnsupportedTarget_Kd`). LLVM's aliases outside the table (`x86_64h`, `i786`, `arm64e`, `arm64ec`) are `unknown`.
  - Rejected: keying the table on `OsType` and `Architecture` (LLVM's prefix and alias matches would give `linuxfoo`, `x86_64h` or
    `arm64e` a family IMPL does not list, and keep a 320-line OS parse for one Condition); a switch per form in Compilation (a
    consumer deciding what the triple's owner publishes).
- **R5-M179 Constant integer tables as little-endian bytes: `IntegerTable<T>` (PLAN G357)** (2026-11-02, the owner: 「(ii) テーブルを byte
  列にして、リトルエンディアンで読み出す」) Major.
  - Cause: under Debug's JIT minopts a constant collection expression of a non-byte element converted to `ReadOnlySpan<T>` compiles to
    `RuntimeHelpers.CreateSpan`, whose `ldtoken` allocates a 72 B `RuntimeFieldInfoStub` per call; Release (tier-0 included) folds it. The
    six generated Unicode tables were such spans, so `Tokenizer.ReadNonAsciiIdentifier` allocated and
    `LexicalLayoutRecoveryTest.OrdinaryIndentationAndUnicodeReuseTokenStorage` measured 1,728 B in Debug. A constant `ReadOnlySpan<byte>`
    is static data in every configuration.
  - Rule: a constant table of integers is stored as little-endian bytes, which its owner publishes as `ReadOnlySpan<byte>`, and its
    one reader wraps them once in `Helper/IntegerTable.cs`'s `IntegerTable<T>` of the element type (`int` or `ulong`, specialized
    by the JIT): `Length` (the element count) and `this[index]` (one range check and one load, as an integer span's; the element's
    bytes reversed on a big-endian host), so the readers index it as before.
  - Tables: `UnicodeIdentifierData.Properties` and `Decompositions` (were `uint`; every value is below 2^31) and
    `UnicodeNameData.SimpleCaseFolding`, `CombiningClasses` and `MarkdownUnicodeData.Punctuation` are read as `IntegerTable<int>`;
    `UnicodeIdentifierData.Compositions` as `IntegerTable<ulong>`. `GenerateNameUnicode.ps1` and `GenerateMarkdownUnicode.ps1` emit the
    byte form (decimal bytes, 24 a line); `UnicodeIdentifierData`, which had no generator, was converted once with every value shown
    equal; since PLAN G738 (2026-11-11) `GenerateIdentifierUnicode.ps1` writes it. Since PLAN G742 (2026-11-11) the three
    generators write the form through one writer, `Add-IntegerTable` in `Helper/IntegerTable.ps1`, which each dot-sources.
  - Departures from the planning session's design, which it took on figures: the read is a `MemoryMarshal.Cast` element, because
    `BinaryPrimitives.Read*LittleEndian` at index × width adds a range check per read; and each reader wraps its bytes, because a typed
    getter (`Int32Table X => new([..])`) is not inlined without PGO.
  - Rejected: (i) `static readonly` arrays (about 83 KB per process) and (iii) Debug `Purpose=Allocation` results as advisory (the owner);
    accessors on each table's owner (the rule spelled in three files and two generators, and wordier readers); a reader type per width
    (`Int32Table`, `UInt64Table`: near-copies of one rule); `IBinaryInteger<T>.ReadLittleEndian` on little-endian hosts (branches on
    length and sign); a `typeof(T)` dispatch through `object` (boxes under minopts, the cause itself).
  - Open: no mechanical rule stops a new non-byte constant `ReadOnlySpan<T>` table, which would bring the Debug allocation back;
    none is added.
- **R5-M180 One owner of the URI a sent location names: `LspSession.UriOf` (PLAN G237)** (2026-11-02, the owner's request to start G237)
  Major.
  - Cause: the server names a document by `SourceIdentity` (`Path.GetFullPath`: 8.3 names expanded, `..` resolved) and published a
    document's list under the URI the client opened it with, but the worker spelled related locations canonically
    (`WorkspaceCheck.Place`, `ToUri()`) and hover links by their file URI (`HoverPlacement.Map`), so a related location or a link into
    a document open under another spelling (an 8.3 name, a `..` segment, another case) opened a second editor; and a document closed
    after its list was sent under the client's spelling had the list cleared under the canonical URI, so the client kept it. The two
    canonical builders also disagreed: `ToUri` (`new Uri(path)`) read a literal `%41` in a file name as `A` and `%2e%2e` as `..`,
    naming another file, where `HoverPlacement.FileUri` escaped it.
  - Rule: `LspSession`, which maps a client URI to its document (`FindOpen`), alone maps a document's identity to the URI it sends,
    `UriOf`: the URI the client opened the document with (the first while it is open; two spellings stay one document), else the
    canonical URI of `SourceIdentity.TryToUri`, the one builder: a built-in identifier's own URI, a path's `file:` URI with `%`, `#`,
    `?` (and a non-Windows `\`) escaped as path data (`FileUri` deleted); none for a path no URI spells (a device path, `\\?\` or
    `\\.\`), whose hover link is shown as text as before, and which a send cannot name (`SentUri` throws, as `ToUri` always did). Every
    location is spelled when it is sent: a publication's URI and related locations (`Publish`, `Spell`), a code action's diagnostics,
    and hover links (`HoverState` and `HoverRenderer` take `UriOf`, which `HoverPlacement.Map` calls with the identity it took for each
    mapped file where the placement was built, so such a link normalizes no path; a link resolved against the project root normalizes
    its path once, as `GetFullPath` did before).
  - Representation: `LspLocation` names its document by identity (`Document`, not serialized) and carries the URI the state owner
    gives it (`Uri`); the worker places identity and range only, so a reused result never carries a stale spelling. A diagnostic
    reaching the sender with an unspelled location is a broken contract (`Spelled`, the one check before both sends, throws
    `UnreachableException`): the JSON context omits a null URI, so it would otherwise be sent silently.
  - Publication: `sent` keeps the placed payload, the spelled one, the version, the URI and the spelling generation, which an open or a
    close advances (`Respell`, which also forgets every HoverState's renderings: a result released unchanged keeps its HoverState). An
    unchanged placed payload under the same generation reuses what was sent and its URI, without spelling or `ToUri` (no allocation);
    otherwise it is spelled, and sent unless equal to what was sent. A list sent under another spelling (the document opened or closed
    since) is cleared there first.
  - Rejected: spelling in the worker from the base's open URIs (reused results and later opens keep a stale spelling); parsing the
    canonical URI back to an identity when sending (a second parse path, an allocation per location); a JSON converter (it cannot see
    the open documents, and repeat suppression would compare unspelled payloads); discarding HoverStates on an open or a close (no
    Hover until the next adoption); keeping `FileUri` beside `ToUri` (two canonical spellings of one file).
  - Unverified: non-Windows hosts (the `\` escape and `TryToUri` there).
- **R5-M181 A publication failure leaves code generation's records (PLAN G157 (7))** (2026-11-02, under R5-M165, R5-M169 and Q13; amends
  R5-M165 with its amendment line) Minor.
  - Cause: `EmissionArtifacts.Publish` checks its inputs (the embedded backend record, paths, native configuration and supplies,
    `LlvmBin`, the output) before code generation and returned at a failure, its record replacing the partition's, so generation never
    ran: its records (a gate step 2 refusal, a code generation `InternalInvariant_Kd` or `Unsupported_Kd`) and its fault were lost.
    Code generation never reads those inputs, so by Q13's rule W its records are independent (SPEC 23.1.2). The converse never
    happened: the inputs are checked first.
  - Rule: a failure before generation still runs generation once, into `TextWriter.Null`, and is recorded after it in a `finally`
    (`FailBeforeGeneration`), since generation clears the partition first; a generation fault so keeps the record beside
    `CheckFaulted_Kd`. `Fail` only reports, so a failure after generation (flush, manifest, replacement) is recorded beside its records.
    Every publication is a generation request (R5-M165's clearing holds: generation clears).
  - Rejected: checking the configuration after generation (a generation fault would hide it, and the backend checks read the embedded
    record); carrying the failure across generation in the method (every path variable needs a placeholder value).
  - Test: `EmissionArtifactsTest.AConfigurationFailureLeavesGenerationsRecords` (an unused non-.lib input and a Drop without a verdict). A
    generation fault beside such a failure was verified by the review's throwaway reflection probe (`CheckFaulted_Kd` and the publication
    record; the base only the latter); no lasting test, since no program makes generation throw without a production seam (R5-M175).

- **R5-M183 A body with a validator finding is no consumer's (PLAN G157 (1), option (a))** (2026-11-03, the owner, verbatim 「(a) で設計を始めて」;
  under SPEC 23.1.2, Q13 and R5-M151) Major.
  - Rule: SPEC 23.1.2 and the owner's (a): only a MIR body that fails validation is excluded; every other body is judged and
    collected. A record that reads such a body (its own A3b checks and layout obligations, an instance it alone requests, a summary
    composed from it) is its finding's dependent. Acceptance never moves: a finding is a MIR record, so check refuses the program.
  - Fact: `MirBody.HasFinding`, the validator's per-body verdict, whose one writer is `MirValidator`: `Validate(body, findings)` sets
    whether it added a finding at each of its three exits (the case bound's, Tables', the end), and `Validate(program)` sets it on the
    ensuring body of a G191 StaticSlot finding. `MirBody.Reset` clears it; tests inject it through the setter. No consumer re-derives
    a per-body set from `MirProgram.Findings`.
  - Collector gates: a body enters `InstanceCollector` at three places, each testing the fact once: the `Templates` walk (an empty
    range, `starts[o]` still written; no A3b check or need listing), the root loop, and `Admit` (-1 after the two checks that read only
    the request, an instance without its substitution and `CarriesInstance`, before `Find`, `Instantiable`, `Grows` and `View`). Every
    other read is of an admitted item's body. A refused request records nothing; `Report` is unchanged.
  - Deletions: `InstanceCollector.Run`'s `Findings.Count > 0` return and its header invariant "a program with validator findings has
    an empty set"; `MirBuilder.Defaults.cs`'s `Findings.Count` difference and its `findings` local (`Failed` reads `this.body.HasFinding`).
  - Staged (U2, R4's `Mir/Analysis/**`): `MirAnalysis.Run` skips a body with the fact in its steps 1, 2 and 4 (`MirDrops.Exclude` closes
    its empty table entry); A4 composes such a body as `Derived` (one private `Views`); the initialization proof that consults one rests
    on it (`Proved` returns `bool?`; `Met` drops only its first block's record and falls through, `Destroying` makes none). Until U2,
    `MirAnalysis.Run` keeps its all-or-nothing `Findings.Count > 0` return (removal condition: U2).
  - Rejected: a body ordinal on `MirFinding` (each consumer re-derives a set), a column on `MirProgram` (a side table), accessors that
    hide broken bodies (a `null` callee silently takes the bodyless path); a validator wrapper or `Check` extraction (a restructuring
    commit for two lines); roots through `Admit` (they would count toward `Grows` and `Work`).
  - Tests: `MirValidatorTest.TheVerdictIsWhetherTheValidatorAddedAFinding`, `AnEnsuredStaticHasItsInitializer`;
    `InstanceCollectorTest.AVersionIsCollectedOnceAndABodyWithAFindingIsNoItem` (was `...FindingsEmptyTheSet`: its expectation changes
    by the owner's (a)), `ABodyWithAFindingDropsOnlyWhatRestsOnIt`, `ARequestsOwnGapAtABodyWithAFindingStays`.
  - Amended (U2, 2026-11-03): the analyses' rule landed as staged. `MirAnalysis.Run`'s `Findings.Count > 0` return, U1's staged part, is
    deleted (its removal condition, U2, holds): a body with the fact closes an empty drop-table entry through `MirDrops.Exclude` (the
    table's one writer) and steps 1, 2 and 4 skip it; A4's one private `Views` composes it as `Derived` at `AddEdge`, `Enter` and `Owe`;
    `Proved` returns `bool?` and `Unproved` `(Fact, Rests)`, so `Met`'s first block and `Destroying` make no record on a proof that rests

    `MirBorrowsTest.ABodyWithAFindingLeavesOtherBodiesProblemsRooted` (the rows that need a live static Loan, which no source program has
    until P42).
  - Amended (GR-1a, 2026-11-04): a second per-body fact, `MirBody.HasConstructionRecord`, whether a construction record lies in the body.
    Its one writer is the builder's one record path of the body in hand, `MirBuilder.Record` (every builder record but a module's broken
    HIR contracts, made before its bodies); `Reset` clears it, and it is read-only after build. A record made without a body in hand
    (those, the collection records) marks no body. The two facts stay apart because `MirAnalysis.Run` reads them apart: it skips a body
    with a finding and analyzes a body with a record. Reader: `Compilation.JudgedWithoutProblem` (hover's ownership line, H0b §2.1), true
    only for a body with neither fact and no merged problem's member. Tests: `VirtualHoverTest`'s
    `OwnershipChecksArePendingForABodyHoldingAConstructionRecord` and `...WithAValidatorFinding` (injected: no source program makes a
    finding); `MirBuildTest.ATupleOperatorWithoutItsComparisonIsUnsupported`, `DefaultExpansionStopsAtTheLimit`.
  - Amended (G157 (1) U-B, 2026-11-06; R5's consent C-59): the Collector gates bullet's "(an empty range, `starts[o]` still written; no
    A3b check or need listing)" now excludes the A3b checks of the body's operations and its need listing, not a static's declaration
    row. The Rule excludes only the failing body; `CheckStatic` reads no body (its `Key` and `Source`, the definition's Type, setter and

- **R5-M186 A3's require fallthrough rests on Binding's guessed nodes (R6-check R6-1)** (2026-11-03, under R5-M182 and Q13) Major.
  - Rule: a require's failure-body fallthrough (A3, `RequireFallthrough_Kd`) is derived from the recovery causes of the nodes Binding's
    guess rule says its completion rests on, as DIAGNOSTICS §4.3 states. A completion that written syntax also reaches stays direct.
    The decisions are split as follows:
    - Binding owns the guess rule. It publishes the guessed nodes (`GuessedCompletionNodes(node, root)`, which allocates nothing) and
      one per-node cause query on that rule's domain, `RestingCauses`. A node outside that domain gets `FailureCauses`, so a resolved
      node has none.
    - The MIR builder records the nodes of `GuessedCompletionNodes(ElseBody, ElseBody)` on the require's `MirMustNotComplete` row, as a
      range into the body's pooled `MirBody.GuessedSites` (`MirOpaque`'s shape).
    - A3 copies each site as a `Cause` fact with Value −1 (the Binding-cause form, R5-M184).
    - MirReport's rule W derives the problem.
    - The publisher's Binding-cause arm names `RestingCauses(site)`. A −1 cause at a node outside the guess rule's domain that has no failure causes,
      such as a node Binding resolved, stays a broken contract (`InternalInvariant_Kd`).
  - The new Mir/Build view (COMPILER_ARCHITECTURE "Dependency rules": "a new view needs a reason in its commit"):
    `Binding.GuessedCompletionNodes`. The reason: which nodes are guesses (bodies the parser supplied, expressions Binding left
    unresolved) and which causes they carry is the guess rule's walk over the pass's completion structure and Never evidence; the HIR
    Completion column publishes only the structural completion itself (the gate below reads it), not the guessed nodes or their
    causes. The builder already visits each require once, and it copies the guessed nodes into the body's pooled storage, so no
    table outside the MIR body holds them. A valid program takes
    Binding's fast path (no recoveries, a complete result) and records no site.
  - Representation: `MirMustNotComplete` gains (Start, Count) into `MirBody.GuessedSites`. A default copy copies no row
    (`MirBuilder.Defaults.Copies.cs`).
  - Before H5 no published record changes. A3's problems publish from H5. The MIR dump `tests/mir/every-form.mir` names its validator
    body's guessed site.
  - Rejected:
    - a catch-all `RestingCauses` ending in the unresolved mark for every node: it hides a broken contract;
    - the publisher asking `GuessedCompletion` at publish time: it would decide dependence, which R5-M184 forbids;
    - a HIR column of guesses per require: a published column for one consumer, held outside the MIR body that reads it, for the same
      walk;
    - re-pointing the tests to a direct record: it weakens DIAGNOSTICS §4.3 and its pins.
  - Cost (review N6): no pass cache in the guess walk. The builder asks only at a failure body whose HIR Completion is not `Diverges`, the
    guess rule's own first test (the same structural completion), so nested requires whose outer failure bodies cannot complete cost no
    walk of theirs. Nested failure bodies that all can complete, in an incomplete pass, stay quadratic in the walk; the old check paid it
    only per falling require.
  - Amended (G47, 2026-11-06; BU, Major, design review Revision 1 ACCEPT): a guess is what StructuralCompletion's guessed walk
    reads and Binding did not establish, whatever the node's BindingState. It is asked only where the walk reads the node itself:
    a block (its items; a guess only when the parser supplied it) and an evaluated node (its Never evidence; a guess when Binding
    did not resolve it and published no Type). A composed form is judged by its parts. This narrows the domain `!= Resolved` that
    held since 8bcc48526, so a written path through a rejected match, if or for keeps its fallthrough direct. Rejected: keying on
    Invalid versus Unresolved (fd88f6625; one failure gets either state).

The bit is a new representation, not a vocabulary entry: `HirAdaptation` stays at 9. Amends R4-M142 ('recorded by `IHirUses.Use(child, in operation)`', its `Claims` of an operation) and R4-M145's finder text only in that the finder takes an operation's use by the same member; BU-8 stands but for its parenthesis "(a PayloadProjection or BaseBorrow states no mode)", which this entry replaces. `LendsExclusively` and `HirAdjust.Of`'s Borrow arm still read `ParameterType`, unchanged.

- **R7-M9 A struct's base clause is read once, `DirectBase`; a read of a clause not ready ends the chain and is counted** (2026-11-08; R7-N2d; Major; design review) SPEC 6.2.2, 8.7.3, 9.4.2, 9.5, 9.6. Extends BU-105 with a row. BU-57, BU-59 unchanged.
  - Rule: `DirectBase(structure)` (`DeclQueryKind.DirectBase`) is the one reading of a base clause as a declaration: its Type's Symbol, else its name under `NoContainer`. `AdtDef.DirectBase` holds a clean read's name or a failed clause's. `BaseLayers` is the one walk, `BaseWalk` its cycle test. "Direct base" is a declaration; "layer" is SPEC's, a Type at a place in the chain.
  - Ready: a clause with a Type, a clause naming a struct, from `clausesBindable` a failed clause. A clause in progress, in the query or in its `BindType`, reads as ended for its own struct. A read of one in progress or not ready ends the chain and counts in `notReadyReads`, and a read that moved the count stores nothing.
  - A name read that saw the count move is noted in `earlyReads` and evaluated again when every clause is final, as it was read. Equal stands. On a difference the declarations run once more (`secondRun`) with `knownBases`, the final Types of the clauses that name no struct. A difference in that run is `Unsupported_Kd` at the use, never a Language error.
  - The records are a function of the source and the mode. Only a first run fills `knownBases`, and a first run starts from none, so they are what a cold Bind of the source and mode computes. A later Bind with both unchanged (`knownMode`, set when a Bind completes; `StartRuns`) starts from them as that cold Bind's second run: it runs once, allocates nothing warm and reports the cold Bind's records. No run's own result seeds the run after it. An edit, a Bind in the other mode and a Bind that did not complete drop them.
  - Temporary, removed at R7-D2 d3 (a conformance's specification read by demand): `clausesBindable`, `notReadyReads`, `earlyReads`, `knownBases`, `knownMode`, `secondRun`, `verifiedClause`, `StartRuns`, `VerifyEarlyReads`, the loop in `Bind`, the second `PublishInheritedOptOuts`.
  - Ends: a recursion passes `DirectBase` (Running, once per struct) or `BindType` (`resolvingTypes`, once per syntax). A chain reads values final in the run; a parameter or a projection through one is no struct and ends it.
  - `BindingSymbol.queries` packs two bits per kind in a `ushort`, in place of the `InlineArray` (a third byte cost 8 bytes a symbol, +12 KB cold on Hello); `DeclQueryKind.Count` makes a ninth kind a compile error. Three states and D2's Error fit.
  - `AdtDef.Base` is null on an inline cycle: an error at the container stands, and no walk reads past it (`c26`, `rx8c`).
  - Removes `memberLookupVisiting`, `qualificationVisiting`, two depth-bounded loops, two recursions, the read's four copies, `DeclStates`.
  - Rejected: a Type in the query's output (binds clauses before associated specifications); a per-declaration array (N² entries); a three-valued `Accessible`; binding by demand now (R7-D2 d3); a clause read that consulted a clause not ready waiting too (`nt42`); `Unsupported_Kd` on a first difference (`rx1`, `j4`); no query state (Chain300 25-27 ms against 19.5 ms); a seed refilled by each Bind's first run (its records alternated, `nt46`); dropping the seed at each Bind (a warm Bind of a second-run program runs twice: +20-34% in design review 2).
- **R7-M10 Access inclusion is decided on SPEC 9.4.2's atoms** (2026-11-08; R7-N3a; Major; no design review, F's ruling 3) SPEC 9.4.1,

    `Body(X) ⊆ Derived(C)` when X is or is nested in a struct deriving from C, `Derived(S) ⊆ Derived(C)` when S is or derives from C.

  - Removes `PrivateDomainWithin` and the lexical-only `protected` arms.

- **R7-M15 One reading of SPEC 9.4.1's table: a use is a point of Body(its Container)** (2026-11-08; R7-N3b; Major; no design
  review, F's ruling 3) SPEC 9.4.1, 9.4.2, 9.4.3.
  - Rule: `AccessUnions(symbol)` is the one reading of the table's rows: the unions a chain's levels give, below the root; a public
    level gives none, a `private protected` level two (Kotonoha(K), then Body(C) ∪ Derived(C)), any other one. A declaration's domain
    is their intersection. `AccessCovers` requires each union of the member's chain to hold, `UnionCovered` finds one union of a's or
    b's chain inside it, and `Accessible` requires each union of the symbol's chain to include the use; no reader splits a row.
  - `UnionIncluded(own, at, union, level)` decides one union inside one union on atoms; it reads a scope: a declaration's own scope,
    or a use's scope read as `private` (a point of Body(its Container); at the root, Kotonoha(K)).
  - SPEC 9.4.3 stays one condition, `ReceiverRuleHolds`: a protected instance member reached only through Derived(C) (the use is not

    Effective Core derives from that struct.

    `private protected` splits (`AccessCovers`, `UnionCovered`, `Accessible`).
  - Rejected: 9.4.3 inside the inclusion (an atom-reporting result, a mode steering it); the row decoded inside `UnionIncluded` (above).
  - Derived(C) of a struct that is not open is empty (SPEC 9.4.1), and Derived follows the declared base clauses (9.4.2): a struct that

  - Extended by R7-M23 (PLAN G610): SPEC 9.4.2's empty intersection of two Kotonoha's atoms covers a union through each chain's

- **R7-M11 `Binding.UseOf`, one place-use rule** (2026-11-08; R7-Y2a, PLAN G251 (1), (3), (5); Major; implementation review ACCEPT, C-136; the owner's O-21 (ii), verbatim 「(ii) で決定」, and O-76 (b) (i), (c) (i), verbatim 「O76は推奨どおりでお願いします」) SPEC 4.7.1, 5.2.1, 7.7.3, 8.14, 15.1.5, 15.1.6. What a use of a Place needs of it (SPEC 4.7.1, 7.7.3, 8.14, 15.1.5, 15.1.6) is decided once, by the Adjust rule: the strongest of the child's two rows' takes (`Take`: ByCase, a bare pair-case acquisition that Reborrows in some case, tested first; Exclusive, an operation's exclusive target, an exclusive borrow or a Reborrow of an exclusive Type; Consuming, a Move) and its parent's own operation, which no row states and which never moves its operand (`BorrowsExclusively`: an exclusive borrow, view upcast or case adaptation in some case; an assignment or update target; an Exclusive-mode Subject). `PlaceUse` is a Binding representation, not a column (O-40 (a): no rows at bind time) and not a HIR vocabulary entry. The HIR publisher reads it for `indexUniq` (ByCase or Exclusive), keeping only its down-propagation, which stops at a raw Place (SPEC 5.2). ClosureEffects reads it over its finder's rows (one `TakesOf`, the shared selection, which `ConsumedByValue` also reads) and owns SPEC 7.7.3's environment rule: past a raw step a Take or in-place destruction needs write capability; `DerivesPointer` is 5.2.1 condition 3's closed list (a displacement, a raw-pointer conversion or fit, an identity conversion; groups are walk steps); the owner's O-76 (c) (i): a pointer read through a raw Place the environment reaches is read from the environment, so the raw rule, `DerivesPointer` and the contract rule apply past a raw step; O-76 (b) (i): a pointer a call with a body returns is not derived (`DerivesPointer` lists no call). A call whose operation contract performs a write-capability access through an argument is the body's access (the owner's O-21 (ii)): the compiler-function table's written inputs, `IntrinsicDisposition.WritesThrough` next to `Effect(kind)` (`RawInitialize` 0, `StorageTransferBytes` 0 and 1, `StorageDestroyValues` 0, `StoragePlaceDictionaryEntry` 0; `Raw.release`, `Raw.slice` none). `StoragePlaceDictionaryEntry`'s row is temporary: R8-K1b gives `placeEntry` a body, and R8-G1 replaces the kind table. A foreign import's contract is prose (SPEC 22.6): its call in any Closure body passed such a pointer is a located `Unsupported_Kd` (`ClosureEffects.Uncontracted`) until imports state their writes; the OQ-1 census found no corpus program. MIR's borrow check decides nothing here; it is the observer that made the two old rules' disagreement an `InternalInvariant_Kd` (N14, h1). Discharges R7-M6's staged sentence ('Y2's `PlaceUse` states a bare take's mode'): `Take` reads the child's Type, and no row field is written. Amends R7-M8's `Claimed` text only in that `Take` replaces `Claims`; BU-8 and Y3's `HirAdjust.Exclusive` stand; D5's selection is per node, under BU-8's open item. **Staged:** Consuming is decided twice, by `Take` (a Move row, read only by the raw rule) and by ClosureEffects' Visit syntax test (the environment's Consuming); removal condition: R7-Y2b folds the second (its Copy-callee move named, SPEC 7.7.3 "A Consuming call Copies a Copy Closure"). Discharged by R7-M12 (R7-Y2b). A pointer copied through a body local stays Shared until R7-Y2c, which reads `DerivesPointer`. **Moves:** h1 `InternalInvariant_Kd` to accepted with `indexUniq`, h3 `InternalInvariant_Kd` to `CallActivationConflict_Kd` (Y2a-2); in a `let` Closure, accepted to rejected (all invalid): a Take or in-place destruction through an environment pointer, a write through a displaced or converted pointer, through `*pp` included (Y2a-3), and `Raw.initialize` through such a pointer (Y2a-4); a foreign import passed one: accepted to `Unsupported_Kd`. **Deleted:** `Claims`, `LendsExclusively`, `NeedsExclusively`' parent switch and recorded-Reborrow clause, the second consumer walk of `ConsumedByValue`, the publisher's Borrow and assignment clauses. **Rejected:** a bind-time column; the raw rule inside the shared fact (5.2); a ClosureEffects case per operation; every or no raw argument of a foreign import counted as written.
  - Discharged by R8-M11 (R8-K1b-2): `StoragePlaceDictionaryEntry`'s temporary `WritesThrough` row; `placeEntry` is a Kimigayo body.
- **R7-M12 ClosureEffects reads `Take` for Consuming, the by-case mark and a nested entry** (2026-11-08; R7-Y2b, PLAN G251's staged sentence; Major; design review ACCEPT and implementation review 2 ACCEPT, F, C-145) SPEC 3.2, 3.5, 7.7.3, 8.14.
  - **The rule.** ClosureEffects reads the one rule, `Binding.Take` (R7-M11), for three decisions: the environment's Consuming, the by-case mark, and a nested entry's need.
  - **Consuming** is a Move by the rule, of the capture or of a stored part of it (Visit's climb).
    - A Consuming call of a captured Copy Closure Copies it (SPEC 7.7.3 "A Consuming call Copies a Copy Closure"), so it no longer makes the outer Closure Consuming.
  - **The by-case mark** is `Take`'s ByCase over both selections (`TakenByCase`).
    - An explicit Transfer of a pair-layer capture is Consuming in every case, no longer by-case Exclusive (SPEC 7.7.3 "A Move on any possible path requires Consuming").
  - **A nested entry's need** is `Take(source Type, nested Closure, BoundCapture.Adjust)`.
  - **Supersedes** R4-M145's by-value list (Copy, Move, Reborrow or ByCase) for the mark. The reason no longer holds: R4-M145 predates `Take`, and its list put an explicit Transfer into the by-case need, against SPEC 7.7.3.
  - **Discharges** R7-M11's staged sentence (Consuming decided twice).
  - **Deleted:** Visit's Consuming syntax test, `ReceiverOperation` and its ProveCopy read, `ConsumedByValue`, `ConsumedTakes.Result` and `ByValue`, `Need.ByValue`, and `VisitEntries`' acquisition switch.
  - **Moves.** Two valid forms are newly accepted:
    - (L1) a Consuming call `k()` of a captured Copy Closure, with the outer Closure called through `ref/F`. Before, an `InvalidAssignment_Kd` at the call.
    - (L4) an explicit Transfer `value@move` of an `owner or uniq` pair-layer capture, whole or a stored part, called `c@move()`. Before, a `StaticMovePathRequired_Kd` at `value@move`.
  - **Records on rejected programs move** (DECISIONS Q13):
    - The bare rule's Move row (a bare Non-Copy or unproven-Copy capture, H1's TransferRequired) now counts as Consuming.
    - The generated gate's p4-like family (`owner or uniq` Transfer under a non-owning call) loses the false `StaticMovePathRequired_Kd` and reports the Consuming call's record.
  - **Rejected:**
    - a Copy-callee clause beside Visit (a second rule);
    - a bind-time failed row for the bare rule's Move (shared across Binding, H1 and MIR, for records on programs already rejected).
- **R7-M13 Pointers derived through a Closure body's locals** (2026-11-08; R7-Y2c, PLAN G251 (1)'s `rv-c-rawcopyptr`; Major; design review 2 ACCEPT, C-147; the owner's O-76 (b) (i), (c) (i) and O-83 (a), verbatim 「O-83 (a)で決定」) SPEC 5.2.1 condition 3, 5.3, 7.7.3.
  - **Definitions.** ClosureEffects records each pointer-typed body local's definitions: an initializer, or an assigned value. A compound displacement keeps the local's provenance (SPEC 5.3). Each definition is recorded by the root that `Below`'s steps descend to.
  - **What each local holds.** `Holds` is Own, Environment, or both. It is computed as one least fixpoint, bounded by the locals.
  - **Roots.**
    - A call's result is its own root (O-76 (b) (i)).
    - A pointer read through a raw Place that the environment reaches is the environment's (O-76 (c) (i)).
  - **A use of a local whose every definition derives from an environment pointer** starts UsesExclusively past its own Place.
    - An assignment of the local is no environment use.
    - Before a raw step, only an operation contract's write through the local counts.
  - **The named limit (O-83 (a)).** A write-capability access through a local whose definitions hold both an environment pointer and a pointer of its own is a located `Unsupported_Kd` at the write's use of the local. It goes through `Undecided`, the one channel for uses whose need no fact decides, shared with the foreign-import call.
    - An Own initializer counts as a definition. So a local initialized from its own allocation and then always overwritten from an environment pointer is Undecided too.
    - Removal condition: Binding publishes its reaching-definitions fact for Closure pointer locals (PLAN G628, a Front unit).
  - **One walk step.** `Below` is the walk's one step in both directions, the climb and `RootOf`'s descent. It replaces `DerivesPointer` and UsesExclusively's three-clause step test.
  - **Cost.** One pass per local. A reverse-ordered assignment chain is quadratic in the worst case, and the scaling row bounds it. A worklist over the definitions by root, about +15 lines and linear, is the named alternative.
  - **Moves.**
    - Invalid programs now rejected with `InvalidAssignment_Kd` at the call: `rv-c-rawcopyptr` and its forms (copy, displacement, conversion, `*pp`, the contract write, `q += 1`, Take).
    - Mixed-definition writes become `Unsupported_Kd`. This includes 9 valid forms that the base accepts, which is O-83 (a)'s named limit. The generated gate has 96 instances over 8 shapes.
  - **Rejected:**
    - a flow-insensitive Exclusive (a conservative Language error on a valid program, which also leaks into every Receiver reader);
    - a bind-time reaching-definitions fact for one classifier. It is deferred to G628 instead.
  - **Open:**
    - pointers held in body-local aggregates, Pattern bindings and `for` slots, which stay accepted on base and head;
    - the generated gate's pre-existing t01-mutate-in-loop and t04-shared-path-for, both invalid and accepted on both sides.
- **R7-M14 An Integer constant's Type is a closed family** (2026-11-08; G620 U2, PLAN G620; Major; design review 1 REVISE, re-check ACCEPT, implementation review 1 ACCEPT, F, C-149; amended 2026-11-09 by G643-G644, PLAN G643-G645: design review and implementation review 1 ACCEPT, the Middle's reviewer, and G645 (the Back's review ACCEPT, C-171)).
  - **Where.** `MirValidator` checks this in `Checker.Holds`, at each Const operand, by MIR's published family `MirTypes.HoldsIntegerConstant`, and code generation reads it in an instance (`FunctionCodegen.Constant`).
  - **The rule.** It accepts an Integer `MirConst` only in these cases:
    1. A Type with a width (`ScalarTypes.Width != 0`). The constant's value is the Type's N-bit payload, sign-extended: `ScalarTypes.Normalize(bits, width) == bits`. BU-133 makes Binding's `Fold` and `TryPatternLiteral` the only encoders.
    2. A widthless Type of the family `MirTypes.HoldsIntegerConstant`: a Type with the integer operators, concrete or generic (`MirTypes.IsArithmeticInteger`, SPEC 13.3.1's set and Binding's name for it: integer arithmetic, an abstract Type, or `Wrapping` over one, which stays constructed until substitution, SPEC 3.1.1, 8.7.4), `char`, or a raw pointer. Its value is ranged: `char` a Unicode scalar value (SPEC 3.1), a raw pointer only null, 0 (SPEC 5.1), and a Type whose instance decides it a generic literal, 0 through 127, a value of every instance (SPEC 8.7.4, BU-133). A literal Binding fits through an identity premise (`T is i32`: 200) has the complete Type, while MIR keeps the premised parameter (BU-72), so it holds by its width under case 1. The integer Cast rows (Integer, Wrap, Numeric, Bits, IntToPointer) read the same `MirTypes.IsArithmeticInteger`.
    3. Any other Type: `MirViolation.Const` (`InternalInvariant_Kd`).
  - **Reason.** Before this entry, no rule held: C-142 N3's 2^127 validated in i32 and in u8. A widthless constant was accepted whatever its Type, a silent default over an open family. The Backend already rejects every other instance Type, so validated MIR now states the same family before code generation does.
  - **Rejected:**
    - accepting every widthless Type;
    - an allowlist of the validator's own, which would be a second rule;
    - a scope-exact parameter test in MIR, which would re-decide Binding's generic-literal rule;

- **R8-M10 A Drop that destroys nothing asks no drop glue** (Back, 2026-11-08; OI-1a, PLAN G641 kinds 1-3; Major; the Middle's C-160
  YES with B1 and B2) SPEC 8.15.3, 14.10.3, 16.2.1, 16.2.2. Supersedes in part R5-M60 (its clause "A2's verdicts do not narrow the
  checked set") and R4-M6a (its clause "a Drop only check edges reach has no row; check-only code is not judged").
  - **Rule.** A check-only Drop has one Elide row where nothing of its Place is initialized on any assumed path, else none, never
    another verdict (A4 relies on it: such a row elaborates nothing, no flag, no codegen, no destructor). `MirDropTable.Elides` is the
    one statement of "this Drop destroys nothing in a view", which A5 (`Dropping`) and the instance collector read; the collector
    requests no DropGlue for such a Drop, and keeps every glue of a body whose verdicts are inexact (`Incomplete`).

    initialize it on the continuation: false `ReassignedLet_Kd`). The temp is made only where `MirTypes.MayNeedDrop` holds,

    elaboration, and an Elide row elaborates nothing.

- **R8-M20 The operator table's comparison domain is one statement, `ComparisonTypes.OperatorCompares`** (Middle, 2026-11-09; PLAN
  G662; Major; design reviews 1 REVISE (B1, B2), 2 ACCEPT; implementation review ACCEPT; the Back's C-187, the Front's C-190; on
  R8-M4's `OperatorTableRuns`; supersedes R8-M15's "Open family" bullet) SPEC 3.1.3, 5.1, 13.4, 13.4.1.
  - **Rule.** `OperatorCompares(type, contract)` (`==` and `!=` under Equatable, the ordering operators under Comparable) is
    `OperatorTableRuns` (the built-in conformances), a floating-point Type's order, a raw pointer's equality and every comparison at
    Never (no value; Binding admits each at a Never terminal). MirValidator's comparison BinaryOp stands only there at its premised
    terminal, or at any abstract operand or Wrapping over one (`MirTypes.IsArithmeticInteger`: MIR reads the shape and trusts
    Binding's proof of the instance); the Never value's unknown Type takes the other operand's; any other is an Operation finding
    (`InternalInvariant_Kd`). The Backend's `Column` reads it under Equatable as the table's domain (every Type with a built-in
    operator has equality) before numbering its columns.
  - **Unit and Never** are in the domain. Neither has a column read: their one value or none needs no operation, and both are
    zero-sized (Never's layout is Unit's), so `Apply`'s zero-sized branch (the row's Reflexive result) is their row.
  - **Staged removal** (the Front's, PLAN G681): Binding's operator rules restate the statement: `ComparisonApplicability` (Never,
    ordered, equality-only arms), `CompleteComparison` (the BinaryOp test), `ComparisonKindOf` and `ComparisonProof` (`operators &&
    IsNumeric`). Removal condition: they read `OperatorCompares`, which also accepts a raw pointer element of a Tuple under `==` and
    `!=` (SPEC 13.4; rejected on dev).
  - **Rejected:** string, struct, enum and Tuple rows (an open family); a validator-local copy of Column's predicates, or of
    Binding's Never row ("a Never terminal is unknown"); widening `OperatorTableRuns` (floats Comparable, pointers Equatable,
    against SPEC 13.4.1); a root operand-class enum that Column maps to columns (moves the Backend's columns out of their owner; no
    second reader yet); a Unit column (no operation).
  - **Moves:** none (no accepted program forms a comparison BinaryOp outside the domain; probes, twins, snapshots).

  - Superseded in part by R8-M25 (G662's remainder): `Column` reads `MirTypes.Operates`, whose comparison rows are
    `OperatorCompares`; the Backend no longer reads `ComparisonTypes`.

  implementation review B1 fixed)
  - `BoundLength`'s tag is Binding's closed `LengthOperation` (Constant, Parameter, Neg, Mul, Div, Rem, Add, Sub,
    InterpolationBound), mapped once from the syntax where a length is bound; its order is `CompareLength`'s (KotoKind's relative
    order of the same forms). No `KotoKind` is added or reused.

    producer is `TyCtxt.InterpolationBound(values, literal)` (R8-W2 a2's builder), folding through `FormattingTypes.StackBound`
    (rule L, `StackLimit` 1,024): a constant when every value Type is closed; 0 when one is decidably unbounded (closed and
    unbounded, or a construction other than `Wrapping`) or the closed values and literal already exceed the limit; else the term

  - Rejected: a `KotoKind` row for the term; forming it in `BindInterpolation` (Binding does not know a line is direct); a reference

- **R8-M23 One Backend walk of a drop group serves the instance collector and code generation (PLAN G641 kind 4)** (Back,
  2026-11-10; R3-U2a, the first part (R3-U1 and R3-U2b extend this entry); Major, no acceptance move, four record moves on rejected
  programs (Q13); design reviews 1 REVISE, 2 ACCEPT; implementation reviews 1 REVISE, 2 REVISE, 3 ACCEPT) SPEC 16.3.2, 15.1.3,
  8.15.3.
  - **Rule.** `DropGlue.Destroyed` (beside `DropGlue.Parts`, in destruction order) is the one statement of what destroying a value
    by a drop group's row destroys, as steps: a Keep, a Flag or (until U2b) an Elide row the value Whole; an Open row an Open step,
    each direct part by its governing row (`Governing`, moved from `FunctionCodegen.Drops` into `DropGlue`'s private walker of one
    group, `Walker`), so an Open part by its own level and any other part Whole, a fixed array's elements from the last as Run steps
    (each run without a row) and element-row steps (`Highest`, likewise), then End. A row of -1 is a glue function's level, which no
    row governs.
  - **The collector** (`InstanceCollector.Destroys`, reading the steps at the template's site, its location and runtime bit) targets
    each Whole and Run step's part (`PartTarget`): at a Drop's site with the site's runtime bit (`DropTargets`; a Drop without a
    group, check-only or of an inexact body, destroys its Type whole), and at a DropGlue item's default site (`DestructionTargets`).
    The `InstanceCollector.Edges` invariant "one target per site" now excepts a Drop's (one per destroyed part, in walk order)
    beside an owner Value call's `Rest`.
  - **Code generation** (`FunctionCodegen.Glue`'s `Destroys`, `Step`, `Opened`) writes a Drop and a glue function's level from the
    same steps, each Whole or Run step reading the destruction's next target (a Drop's site range, checked consumed; a glue
    function's own item's); its former per-level traversal (`DestroyParts`, `Cases`, `Part`, `Elements`, `DestroyByRow`) is gone.
  - **Why.** The collector requested an Open Drop's whole-Type glue, whose admission requests every part's glue, while codegen
    destroys only what the group leaves (the cause of G641 kind 4, with U1's check-only groups); one walk read by both makes U2b's
    "skip Elide rows" a change of one statement.
  - **Moves.** No acceptance move; records move on four rejected programs (+`InvalidCLayout_Kd` x4, DECISIONS Q13; the Back's
    revision 3): `T_deadRet`, `T_deadFlag` and `T_deadRetAll` at 12:5, `I_deadOpenU` at 8:18 (an Open Drop now requests its parts'
    glues, and a refused item reports where it is first requested); `T_deadRetAll` is valid and already rejected on dev by this
    row's cause, and U2b accepts it. Snapshot 0 and natives equal. Generated IR: a partly moved value's whole-Type
    `__kimi_drop<item>` leaves the module where nothing else requests it, and item indices renumber.
  - **Rejected:** the prototype's collector-only walk (a third copy of A4's walk, out of destruction order, with a 64-part bit set);
    codegen restating the walk's composition (implementation review 1's U1); moving the part order to Mir so A4 shares the walk (a
    larger unit; recorded in the design).
  - **R3-U1: a check-only Drop's group is what it would destroy; A4 runs none** (Back, 2026-11-10; Major, no acceptance or record
    move; B's design reviews 1 REVISE, 2 ACCEPT; the Middle's design review (C-195) REVISE, B1-B3, and RP17 consent YES;
    implementation reviews: B's REVISE (S1) and the Middle's REVISE (B1′), both ACCEPT on the fix commit) SPEC 14.10.3, 16.3.2,
    15.1.3, 8.15.3. Supersedes in part R8-M10 (its rule "a check-only Drop has one Elide row where nothing of its Place is
    initialized on any assumed path, else none, never another verdict").
    - **Rule (A2, `MirDrops`).** A group says what its Drop destroys, stated once in `MirDropTable`'s summary, which every walk of
      it cites: a Keep or Flag row its Type whole (its drop, then every part); an Open row its child rows, its parts without a row
      and a base without one, never a drop of its own; an Elide row nothing. A Drop only check edges reach with a Move Path gets a
      group from the state on its assumed paths, by the same per-view Type rule; one without a Move Path has none.
    - **One site for the check-only reading (`MirDrops.Tree`).** `Record` records the same state tree whatever the reach, and the
      Drop's reach beside it; `Tree` reads a check-only group there alone: flagless (Flag's state reads as Keep, no row has a flag;
      check-only code has no flags, R4-M6a), and where an Open layer's Type declares a `drop` (it may be incomplete where that drop
      would run, SPEC 15.1.3, 16.3.2), the one condition gives `MovedPlace_Kd` at a runtime Drop (the body inexact, as before) and,
      in a check-only group, which is not judged (R4-M6a's clause, kept), a **Keep** row with no child rows: its whole destruction,
      its `drop` included, exactly dev's checked set there (SPEC 8.15.3 paragraph 2: no SPEC reading destroys such a layer without
      its `drop`).
    - **A4 (`MirEffects.Dropped`).** A Drop only the checks reach runs no destructor, whatever its group (one gate, `flow.Runtime`).
    - **Readers.** Codegen generates only the blocks the runtime walk reaches (`FunctionCodegen` I3), so it reads runtime groups
      only; A4 gates check-only ones; A5's `Dropping` reads `Elides`, which now also holds on check-only Drops whose Type needs no
      drop (where `Destruction` is shallow; A5 neutral: the A5 class set passes, snapshot 0); the instance collector still asks the
      whole glue for a non-Elide group until U2a/U2b.
    - **Moves.** None in acceptance or records (U1 alone; snapshot 0). The dump shows check-only groups (the `tests/mir` goldens and
      `MirDropTest`'s rows, listed in the commit).

    at any are broken contracts. MirValidator's UnaryOp and BinaryOp stand only where it holds at the left operand's premised
    terminal (the right one's after a Never-value left), else an Operation finding (`InternalInvariant_Kd`); the Backend's `Column`
    reads it for each operator it applies (a statement's, an arithmetic shim's, each comparison of a Builtin leaf).

    `IsLeft`) under its contract header; Binding's `ArithmeticContractSyntax` (`Binding/ArithmeticContractSyntax.cs`) keeps what

- **R8-M28 The library's size is stated once: `KimiLibrarySize`** (Back for the Front, 2026-11-10; R8-W1c-2a, board C-210 (A), the
  Front's design reviews, re-check and implementation review; the owner's O-136 (a) and O-139 (a)). Every compilation's tables hold
  the library's entries beside the program's and grew by doubling from small capacities, so each library unit moved a table's
  doubling into a cold scaling row's window. `KimiLibrarySize` states the library's entry count, rounded up to a Granule of 1,024,
  in each per-compilation table it sizes, and three kinds of room: `NodeRoom` (8,192) in the node table, `KeyedRoom` (1,024) in a
  keyed table, and none in a library-only table (member selections, capability nodes), which starts at its stated count. A table
  with a room starts at its stated count plus that room, so after a Bind of the library alone it keeps the room free;
  `KimiLibraryShapeTest` checks the statement (`TheStatedSizeIsTheLibrarys`) and the room of the tables that have one
  (`TheLibraryLeavesEachSizedTableItsRoom`). Selection is by bytes, not by entries: a table is sized when, grown by doubling from
  empty, the doubling that follows the library's fill would allocate more than 64 KB, of which three fit inside the smallest margin
  of the cold scaling rows (nine tables). The rooms are sizing facts, not contracts: a program past a room, or one that fills a
  library-only table's free slots, may double that table.
  - **The library-only kind, a known limit (the Front's R1; the owner's O-139 (a), verbatim 「(a) e のまま着地する」):** the kind was chosen
    because no cold scaling row's program adds an entry to either table; that is its reason and no guarantee. Programs fill both: a
    member access adds one member selection, a Copy struct declaration two capability nodes. So each table's next doubling (139,980
    B and 102,652 B, above the selection rule's 64 KB) sits where the library's fill puts it, and the unit moves it: a member-read
    row of the tests' shape (cold Bind bytes at 128, 256 and 512 reads, factor 3) measures 1.100 on dev 53cf29caf and 3.118 on this
    unit. No row of the suite reads a member or declares a Copy struct. The RP8 exception below covers this limit until the removal
    condition holds.
  - Supersedes `DeclarationTableCapacity` (b7488ebfe, board C-124): its reason, one fixed size reviewed when the library grows, no
    longer holds, since each library unit moved a table's doubling into a scaling row.
  - **RP8 exception (the owner's O-136 (a), verbatim "(a) Land as exception", and O-139 (a)):** the unit lands although Hello's cold
    Bind median is slower than RP8 allows. B's T-100, 12 pinned rounds: Hello cold Bind median +4.5% against an A'/A spread up to
    +1.7%; cold min and warm Bind equal; cold bytes -3.0%, large-object bytes -5.3%, gen2 collections 16 against 17 per 60 Binds;
    retained bytes +4.8%. By the trace's reading (B's trace; the median's attribution in milliseconds was not measured), the slower
    cold median is the collector's cadence in a multi-compilation loop, not Bind work: blocking gen1 collections that fall before
    the next large-object gen2 promote the dropped compilations' graphs, 12-21 MB against 3 MB.
  - **Removal condition:** R8-L1 (a frozen library: no compilation rebuilds tables holding the library's entries), if RQ13 adopts it
    (the plan's RQ13 thresholds). Until R8-L1 removes it, this statement, its two tests and the RP8 exception stand.

    every library unit); a capacity or a room per table; one room for every table (U) and two rooms over six tables (H); `KeyedRoom`
    2,048 with or without the library-only kind (revision 2, d: more large-object bytes and gen2 collections); selection by entry
    count (it admitted a table whose step is smaller than an excluded table's).

  destruction walk composes it with a group's rows, and the builder and the Backend read it (PLAN G702)** (Back with the Middle's
  consent, board C-212; Major: a contract across phases; no acceptance, record or IR move).
  - **Supersedes in part.** R8-M23's rule that "`DropGlue.Destroyed` … is the one statement of what destroying a value by a drop
    group's row destroys" (its `Walker`, `Governing`, `Highest`) and its rejected option "moving the part order to Mir so A4 shares
    the walk (a larger unit)"; **R5-M95's reading of `DropGlue.Parts` as "the one enumeration the collector's DropGlue items target
    and FunctionCodegen.Glue writes from"**: the one enumeration is now `MirDropTable`'s walk, which `DropGlue.Destroyed` and
    `DropGlue.Level` map; `DropGlue.Parts` keeps only the parts no move path names (a declared destructor, a collection's element

    of a destructor body stands and now reads the fact.
  - **Rule.**
    - **The fact and its owner.** `MirTypes.LevelCount(type)` and `MirTypes.LevelPart(type, rank)` (`Mir/MirTypes.Destruction.cs`,
      the Type facts' owner) are the one statement of SPEC 16.3.2's level order: a Type's direct parts in destruction order, by
      rank, as move-path steps (a Tuple's elements and a Closure's captures from the last; a fixed array's elements from the last;
      an enum's Case payloads by ordinal; a struct's Fields in reverse declaration order, then its direct base). Body-independent:
      no body, row or verdict is read. A rank no part has is a broken contract (`InvalidOperationException`, InternalInvariant).
      `MirBody.PartType` gives a part's Type.
    - **Its readers.** `MirDropTable.Destroyed` (a group's walk: the level composed with the group's rows) and `MirDropTable.Level`
      (the level no row governs, a glue function's) in `Mir/Analysis/MirDrops.Destroyed.cs`, as `MirDropStep`s (built only by
      `MirDropStep.Whole`, `Run`, `Open`, `End`; no optional parameter, CR-R2); a fixed array's elements are walked down from the
      first rank's position to the last rank's, both read from the fact, each run of elements without a row one Run step.
      `MirBuilder.FieldCleanup` (a destructor body's cleanup of its layer's parts) reads the fact and keeps only its own filter
      (`MirTypes.MayNeedDrop`) and its `DropAt`: the builder reads no analysis. A4 (`MirEffects.Dropped`) reads each Whole and Run
      step's Type, as a set. The Backend maps: `DropGlue.Destroyed` and `DropGlue.Level` map each step to its glue part (the
      aggregate writer's position, a Case's ordinal) and state no order of any aggregate's parts; a Case payload destroyed whole is
      mapped through `MirDropTable.Level` of the payload Tuple under the payload's rows.
    - **The census by search.** Every iteration over a Type's parts in `Mir/**` and `Backend/**` (every reverse loop, every loop
      over a Type's components, Case payloads, captures, Fields or length) is classified: the fact; reads the fact; not a
      destruction order, with its rule; kept with its reason. No copy of SPEC 16.3.2's level order remains. Kept: `DropGlue.Parts`'
      collection element Types (not a level; read as a set); a Run's direction (`MirDropStepKind.Run`'s definition, which cites the
      fact, and the Backend's Run loop that realizes it).
    - **The walk's cost.** A walk reads the rows below its row in two passes (their count; their index, each row under its parent
      row and its part's key, sorted once), then searches the index once per part of an Open level: linear in the group's rows at
      any width and depth but for the sort and the searches' logarithm (bounded by `MirDropTest`'s width and depth rows). A row with
      nothing below builds no index.
    - **The child-row contract.** A child row of an Open row names a direct part of that row's Type: `MirDropTable`'s contract, met
      by A2's writer by construction; the walk and `MirValidator` check nothing (an assertion, if ever wanted, belongs at A2's row
      creation as `InternalInvariant_Kd`).
  - **Why.** A4 and the Backend each derived the destroyed parts from the Type and the rows, a glue function's level restated the
    same order, and the builder's Field cleanup stated the struct level a third time; the order is a language rule about a Type, so
    it is a Type fact, and Mir is the only place every reader reaches.
  - **Rejected:** keeping `DropGlue.Parts`' aggregate arm for glue functions beside Mir's walk for groups; the Backend's own loop

    walk (Mir/Build would read an analysis); a level scanning its whole subtree for its child rows; an index keyed by a rank (the

    the Backend's stated in Mir's level, not of the order. The instance collector requests the element's glue from that Run and code
    generation reads that target for `[0 of T]`; it writes no loop (the Run has no element), so the checked set and generated code

  implementation review 1 ACCEPT (B's reviewer); extends R8-M31).

    `MirProgram.LibraryCount` - 1, and the program's follow. `MirBuilder.Build` builds the library's module first (its default
    templates, then its bodies), calls `EndLibrary`, then builds the source modules (templates, then bodies). Templates still
    precede their copiers, because a library body omits library defaults only.

    - `MirProgram.Body(ordinal)` reads either segment. It is the one read by ordinal.
    - `MirProgram.Bodies` is the compilation's own bodies, which walkers iterate. While a compilation builds its library's bodies,
      it includes the prefix.
  - No reader offsets an ordinal or computes one from `LibraryCount`.
  - Walkers of `Bodies`: `MirAnalysis.Run`, `MirValidator`'s program pass, `MirOrigins.Findings`, `MirDump.Write`, and
    `InstanceCollector`'s roots and templates; the Benchmark's counts (`CompilerPipelineBenchmark`, `CollectionCostMeasurements`,
    `PairCaseMeasurements`, `StaticKeyMeasurements`) also read it. U5b changes `Bodies` to the program's suffix, in one edit, and
    the Middle's A/B states the Benchmark counts' new meaning.
  - `MirDump.Write(body, ...)` reads `body.Ordinal` for A2's table, instead of taking the ordinal as a parameter (R3-N6).
  - Rule: `MirProgram`'s contract. `MirBuildTest.TheLibrarysBodiesAreTheOrdinalsPrefix` checks it; `MirValidator` does not.
  - Staging:
    - U5b: the prefix comes from the frozen library. `MirDropTable` and the collector's site templates (`sites`/`starts`,
      `needs`/`needStarts`) split at L there, folded into U5b (B, 2026-11-11), so no temporary writer path is added in U5a.
    - U5c: A4's `bases` and node and Field segments, with its frozen base.
  - Behavior-preserving: no output moves (evidence in the commit). A4's node ids now put the library first (its worklist is seeded
    in node order), which U5c builds on. `MirEffects.Evaluations` (a measured count, not output) may change with that order, so
    `StaticKeyMeasurements` and the Middle's A/B attribute it to U5a-1.
  - Rejected:
    - a physical two-segment layout of every table now, with both segments built per compilation: a temporary writer path that U5b
      would remove;
    - a `MirValidator` check of the prefix: the owner assigns the ordinals, so the rule holds by construction.

    into the leaf, which then stays out of line at every caller (T-152: Interpolation O2 B/A 1.128).

    compares as one value: part of its identity because `Define` reuses a signature and `GetDefinition` caches its text, and one
    operand of its chain however many flags join; calls are unchanged; inert at O0 (no opt pass).

    reservation, where S2d1's leaf had the whole chain inlined (one call site at every level); A, the runtime path, also called its
    reserve once per write there, so this is no cost against A. S2d1's advantage there is smaller than the call count says: with the

    at once (no source is established or parsed, though the resolver has read every node's sources, and no phase runs;

    when `AnalyzesNoModule` is false, and `Compilation.Check()` never runs on such a Compilation.

    decoded other syntax with no diagnostic. A limit is a Resource diagnostic (IMPL 21.3.2, A.4; SPEC 23.1.1), and the result is
    Completed, not Blocked: Blocked is an input that could not be established, explained by an Input error (SPEC 23.2.2).
  - Rejected: running the phase sequence over no module (a false `MissingStartupBody_Kd`); inferring the outcome from an empty
    `SourceModules` at each reader (the test-presence answer was No for sources never parsed); widening the ordinal to `int`
    (supersedes R8-M31's constant across the three areas and leaves the count unbounded); a known limit (the silent wrong decode
    stays, against IMPL A.3 and A.4); an internal invariant at the narrowing cast (a valid program over an implementation limit is
    Resource, not Internal).
  - Tests: `DependencyConfigurationTest.ModuleCountIsLimitedBelowTheLibraryOrdinal` (65,535 accepted, 65,536 refused);
    `HoverCollectionTest.OptionalCollectionKeepsAModuleCountRefusal` (65,536 modules through `CheckService`, with and without hover:
    Completed, the one record at the root project file, test presence Unknown, no hover fault).
- **R9-M1 A check's phase sequence is `Compilation.Check`** (2026-11-08; R9-F5; Major, behavior-preserving; review 1 REVISE, then
  review 2). SPEC 23.1.2, 23.2.2; IMPL 20.6.1. Supersedes in part R5-M65 (`Project` reads `Accepts`) and R5-M77 (`Project` discovers
